1d6+6 Scraps (25c) from enemies there (Hand In). Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months).
1$
An inventor approached a military grade weapon's facility with a prototype weapon. The weapon was so powerful, if it 
ever got constructed it would be a planet-killer. However, whilst the plans were en route a galactic peace activist posing 
as a security guard stole them and hid them inside a security pass. Their intention was to destroy the plans at a later 
time, away from preying eyes. However, there was a mix up and the security pass with the plans got thrown out and 
taken to a dump site, where it is now lost.
SECURITY BREACH (AM O2): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to enter a dump site and 
Collect (Hand In) 1 Security Pass with the hidden plans, or 1 Objective Item (see operation for details). Expires: 
[DATE] (1 month).
If the star system you generate for the mission's location has a moon, or a dead planet point of interest, then this is 
the zone where the mission is located. If the system has both a moon and a dead planet, you must generate randomly 
between them where the mission will be located. If the system has neither a moon, or a dead planet then you must 
generate a random empty zone where the mission will be located. 
Whilst on the away mission if the captain gains a security pass, it may be the pass with the hidden plans, and you roll 
1d100 to check; if the result is 30 or less then it's the security pass with the hidden plans and the away mission is com-
pleted. Note: If the captain finds a batch of security passes (i.e. the game instructs +2 Pass, or +3 Pass), you do not check 
each individual pass, but instead make one roll for the entire batch. Alternatively, the first Objective Item the captain 
finds is in fact the security pass with the hidden plans and the mission is completed.

The port's authorities are offering a special bonus to starships trading depleted goods.

A mining operation has come to an end and the miners need transport back home to their families.
TRAVEL HOME (SM): Pick up 1d6+6 x 10 passengers in zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system and get them back home 
(see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d3+2 months).
Add the generated number of passengers that need to be picked up to the zone where the mission is located. The captain 
may pick up any number of passengers (life support permitting) whenever the captain is in the zone. For each passenger 
that is added to the starship, roll for their destination in the usual way and record them to the passenger manifest. Then 
reduce the number of passengers that need picking up by the number you have added to the starship. When the number 
of passengers that need picking up is reduced to 0 you have completed the mission and the captain receives the reward.

Rifters are an ancient order going back six millennia. They use mind control and telekinesis to perform all kinds of 
strange and mystical effects. The Rifter Program was created in the last century and outlaws the use of Rifter "Wizardly" 
in all but a few star systems. Wherever the program is upheld, the Rifters have moved underground and are still prac-
ticing their powers. Rifters practice a lot with military grade enduring tonics, mixing them and adding to them, and are 
often on the look out for anyone selling them; the older the better. There is an abandoned weapon's factory that may 
have some old enduring tonics lying around, and you know of a Rifter that may be interested in buying them!
ENDURING (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] and also a Rifter wants you to enter the facility 
and Collect 1d3 Enduring items from tables TA, TB, or TC (results 79, 89-92,97) (Hand In). Expires: [DATE] (1d3+1 month).

the zone where the mission is located. If the system has both a moon and a dead planet, you must generate randomly 
between them where the mission will be located. If the system has neither a moon, or a dead planet then you must 
generate a random empty zone where the mission will be located.
4$

safety protocols malfunctioned. Now they are running amok and need to be destroyed.

A smuggler with contacts to an organized crime syndicate is looking for someone to move some goods.
NARCOTICS (SM): [NPC] wants you to collect 2d10+40 units (tons) of narcotics from zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] 
system and drop off to zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1 month).
When you generate the star system where the narcotics are to be dropped off, it must be in a different star system to the 
one where it is collected (re-roll if you generate the same star system). The captain can collect and deliver the narcotics in 
any quantity they like. As they're delivered you can keep track of how much is left to transport by changing the mission's 
details (i.e. if you have 40 units remaining to transport, and drop off 25, you change the mission's details to say "...Collect 
15 units...") As soon as the captain picks up the first load of narcotics the captain gains +1 Law. When all narcotics have 
been transported the mission is completed and the captain gains the reward. If you have begun the mission, but it expires 
before it is completed, someone in the crime syndicate has tipped off the authorities, see the Tracked Down event.
4$
"There used to be a small moon in that sector of space. However, the cyborg destroyed it and fragments are now scat-
tered all over the star system. One chunk still has an old mining facility. It is essentially a floating rock over a hundred 
miles wide that you can land on and get inside. Once inside the mine, its just a case of locating the artefact. I would pay 
dearly to just see it and perform a few scans for my research, then its yours to keep."
ARTEFACT (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Collect a powered item from table 
TA, TB, TC (results 99-100); or 1d3+1 Objective Items (convert to result 99 on table TA). Expires: [DATE] (1d6 months).
For background information on the Cyborgs, see Mission # 95-96, History of the Cyborgs in the main D100 Space rulebook.
4$
"In a hidden chamber in the lower levels of the space port is a bag loaded with credits. I know, because I hid them there 
about 25 years ago. You are welcome to the cash, I just need that bag returned to me!"
LOWER LEVEL (AM O2 NV): At [PORT] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Explore until you have descended to 
a lower level and searched an Objective Area (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (2d10+10 Days).
You may begin the away mission during a port phase. When performing the away mission the captain must find an 
Emergency Staircase. This can be achieved by either by rolling 88-90 on table G - Geographic when generating a green 
area; or alternatively one may be found when the captain searches an area; each time the captain searches an area, you 
can roll 1d100. On a result of 10 or less an Emergency Staircase is found (refer to result 88-90 on table G - Geographic 
for details). Once the staircase has been added to the map sheet, the captain must descend to a lower level, and find 
and search an Objective Area to complete the mission.
4$

through political manipulation, but in some cases by force. Recently, they have unlawfully kidnapped a leader of the Rebel 
Might and taken them to a secret base for questioning over charges of espionage. Once the questioning is over the rebel

him in trouble, but this time he has taken things too far and has attacked a supervisor. The ports authorities have put 
out a bounty out for his capture.
UNHAPPY WORKER (AM NV): At [PORT] in the [SYSTEM] system after a port phase Explore until 1d3+1 blue areas

A fugitive is being hunted by two bounty hunters. The bounty hunters are acting independently and are in a race with 
one another to find and kill the target. Unfortunately for the fugitive, both bounty hunters are Hunterpeds; an evil alien 
race who have a savage reputation to skin their targets alive and slowly torture them to death. Needless to say it has 
now become a situation of kill or be killed.
THE BOUNTY HUNTERS (SM): In the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to track down two bounty hunter starships 
and destroy or capture them (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months).
Whenever the captain is in a zone in the mission's star system, they may search for a bounty hunter starship by per-
forming the SCANNING test below. If the test is passed successfully the captain has located the zone where one of the 
bounty hunter's starship can be found and you roll 1d10 for its zone. Unless the captain is already in that zone, they 
must then head there to attack it. The captain must move directly there, and may not perform any other actions on the 
way. If they do perform an action before reaching the zone, the bounty hunter starship may have moved on and the 
SCANNING test must be repeated.
SCANNING - Test: Int -20, +/- CM, +/- DT [S: -1 AP, -1 PL, roll 1d10 for a zone where the bounty hunter starship is located] 
[F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Navigators). 
When the captain is in the zone with a bounty hunter starship see the Space Battle event. The captain must destroy or 
capture both bounty hunter starships to complete the mission and receive the reward.
4$
A few months ago a starship crash landed on a small moon. The captain and his entire crew were killed instantly, leaving 
no survivors. With no next of kin, the starship is now covered by galactic salvage laws and salvage teams have been 
picking away at its contents ever since its crash. An old army buddy who served with the deceased captain during the 
Royal Wars would like the his medals as a keepsake. They are fixed to a piece of armour the captain always wore in 
battle. The armour is yours to keep, all they want are the medals.
ARMOUR (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Collect powered armour from ta-
ble TA, TB, TC (results 99); or 1d3+2 Objective Items (convert to result 99 on table TA). Expires: [DATE] (1d6 months).
If the star system you generate for the mission's location has a moon point of interest, then this is the zone where the 
mission is located. If the system doesn’t have a moon point of interest then you must generate a random zone where 
the mission will be located (see Random Star Systems and Zones).
4$
From a bygone age, when cyborg labour was commonplace a prototype shield was being developed at an armour 
facility on a small moon. The Cyber Wars put pay to cyborg labour and the facility fell into disrepair and is no longer 
used. It is now overrun with all kinds of villainy and scum. However, the prototype shield known as the "Cyborg Shield" 
is somewhere in that facility and just waiting for someone foolish enough to go looking for it!
THE CYBORG SHIELD (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system Collect any Energy Shield from table A (it 
gains +1 ES, +100c); or 1d3+2 Objective Items (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d6 months).
If the star system you generate for the mission's location has a moon point of interest, then this is the zone where the 
mission is located. If the system doesn’t have a moon point of interest then you must generate a random zone where 
the mission will be located (see Random Star Systems and Zones).
If you exchange Objective Items to gain the Energy Shield roll 1d3+1 to generate the Energy Shield's (ES) value. The 
energy shields credit value is its ES value multiplied by 100 (i.e. (ES2) = 200c, (ES3) = 300c etc.)
4$

A criminal with contacts to an organized crime syndicate is taking matters in hand and has non-officially requested

Expires: [DATE] (1d3+2 months).
Using table (GB) C - Cargo Prices reset the [ILLEGAL] buy and sell values at [PORT] on the economy sheet using the +4$

A tyrannical galactic powerhouse known as "The Royal Command" has set in motion a deadly plan to take control of 
the [SYSTEM] system. They have constructed a secret base on a dead planet within a star system, and have in place 
thousands of troops and a large fleet ready for the attack. The base is now ready for the invasion and is just waiting for 
a General of The Royal Command to arrive to launch the attack. Meanwhile a member of the Rebel Might, has been 
dispatched to the star system and has been given the authority to reward anyone who brings them the general's head.
THE GENERAL (AM NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Explore until 1d3+2 blue areas 
have been found. The last blue area is the Objective Area (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (2d10 +10 days).

Microaliens have infested a water supply at a water collecting base. The infestation is spreading fast and needs some-
one to enter the plant and fit a special eradication devise to each of the filtration tanks. It is dangerous work as the 
plant has been out of operation for so long whilst the infestation was investigated that all manor of villainy and scum 
have breached its containment field.
WATER FILTERS (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system Explore until 1d3+6 green areas have been 
searched and had an eradication devise fitted (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d6 months).

the mission is located. If the system doesn’t have a water world point of interest then you must generate a random zone

water world point of interest, until the mission is completed, or has expired, no water may be collected from the water 
world. As a reminder place a cross above the point of interest until the restriction no longer applies.

something of a bygone era. They were built by explorer civilizations to establish space posts in pockets of deep space. 
Thousands can be found all over the galaxy in various states of repair. This particular space moon needs hundreds of 
starships to bring in materials from all over the galaxy, so it can once again re-establish itself as a working community 
with a self-sufficient population. Each starship will receive a nice bonus too.

Abundance:
Across the sector there has been a huge increase of goods be-
ing sold on the open market. Trade ships have been selling a lot 
and it has affected the economy.
Using the numbers at the top of the Economy Sheet, roll 1d100 
to select what commodity is affected. The targeted commod-
ity is now being sold all over the sector and it has affected its 
trade prices. Using table (GB) C - Cargo Prices reset the affect-
ed commodity's buy and sell value for all star systems that 
have been added to the economy sheet using the -4$ row.
Alien Attack:
Your scanners pick up multiple starships dropping out of warp and 
moving towards several points of interest. The ships are alien in 
origin. Their like have never been seen before in this part of the 
galaxy and the sheer number of them looks like an invasion force. 
Add "ALIEN ATTACK" to the star system's hex 
where the captain is currently at on the hex 
sheet. Next, add a trigger arrow g to the cur-
rent star date and then make the following date 
entry: "[DATE] The [SYSTEM] system is under a 
savage alien attack. When entering the [SYS-
TEM] system roll 1d6, if you roll a 6, a ship at-
tacks, see the Ship Attacks event." 
Then, shade the star date 1d3 months and 
2d10 days in the future and make the follow-
ing date entry: "[DATE] An alien attack in the 
[SYSTEM] system comes to an end, see the Al-
ien Attack event."
When the event comes to an end, remove the 
ALIEN ATTACK from the system's hex. Then, 
find the trigger arrow on the Star Date Chart 
relating to the alien attack and place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger ar-
row g from the star date; it no longer applies.
Note: When you're recording date entries re-
place [SYSTEM] with the name of the star system 
affected in all cases.
Ancient Shrine:
As you're about to leave and head back to the ship, your scanner 
goes berserk. You follow the readings and it leads you to a hole in 
the ground. You peer in and can see a room down there, with what 
appears to be a Ancient Shrine. 
If you wish the captain to investigate the shrine before they 
return to the ship, they must lower themselves down into the 
room. Perform the LOWER test below. If the test is successful the 
captain reaches the bottom of the room safely; otherwise, they 
have fallen and suffer -1d3 HP. The captain is then able to interact 
with the shrine; see Shrine Interaction below. When the captain 
has finished interacting with the shrine, they will need to climb 
out of the room and you must perform the CLIMB test below un-
til it is passed successfully.
LOWER - Test: Str [S: Bottom reached] [F: Fall, -1d3 HP, bottom 
reached] (Strong)
CLIMB - Test: Dex [S: Top reached] [F: Fall, -1d3 HP] (Agility)
Shrine Interaction
The shrine is on a raised platform with a life-sized figure of an al-
ien creature standing in the middle. All around the alien are circles 
etched into the platform. When the captain begins investigating 
they find a long inscription which they read aloud. As soon as the 
last words are spoken light erupts from the circles and an object 
phases into view. Roll 1d6 below to see what has appeared.
1.	
Roll on table N - Needed.
2.	
Roll on table A - Armour.
3.	
Roll on table W - Weapons.
4.	
Roll on table TA - Trappings A (re-roll results of 1-30).
5.	
Roll on table TB - Trappings B (re-roll results of 1-30).
6.	
Roll on table TC - Trappings C (re-roll results of 1-30).

Arena
You can feel the excitement in the air. One of the arenas is being 
opened later today and tickets are half price. The buzz is every-
where and it would be a shame to miss out. The arena is usually 
a great deal of fun and has a lot going on. Acts vary from star 
system to star system; however, they all follow a general trend 
with performances of opera, modern music, comedy, dance, acro-
batics, mime, magic etc.
The base cost of a ticket is 100c you must then augment the cost 
by the current star system's reward adjustment x10. 
Example: Jacob is at a space station in a poor star system. The 
system's reward adjustment is -2 $. He multiples -2 x 10 for a total 
of -20. He buys the ticket for 80c (100-20=80).
When the ticket has been bought and you have deducted the cal-
culated number of credits from the log sheet shade 4 Action Pips 
(AP) on the action tracker, and then roll 1d6 on the list below to 
see how the arena visit went.
1.	
The captain is robbed, see the Robbed event.
2.	
The captain is attacked, see the Hostile event.
3.	
The captain meets someone, see the Romance event.
4.	
The captain is enticed to some gambling at the arena's bar, 
see the Gambling event.
5.	
The captain overhears a rumour, see the Rumour event.
6.	
The captain's spirits are lifted (+1 Karma).
Arrengale
The Arrengale are a race of free roaming galactic space pirates. 
They have no home world, no government, or political structure. 
They fly through space along ancient migration routes they have 
used for centuries; living off space as they go, and stealing what-
ever they need to survive. Their ships are impressively large, and 
fitted with high tech weaponry and advanced defence systems. 
You check the scanner again and again and then sigh nervously. This 
is not going to end well. An Arrengale vessel has just dropped out 
of warp and is arming its weapons. Then, a voice calls out over the 
comms, "Surrender your vessel." The voice is calm and has a strong 
Arrengaley accent. "Lower you shields and prepare to be boarded. If 
you resist we will destroy you." The ship is ten times the size of the 
largest ship you have ever seen and you count twenty forward phaser 
cannons and ten particle beams. You have no choice but to surrender.
Roll 1d100 and deduct the current star system's threat level. If 
the result is 10, or less the Arrengale pirates take the captain's 
starship and sell the captain into slavery, see the Sold Into Slav-
ery event. If the result is 11 or more continue reading.
The Arrengale pirates strip the captain's ship back to its bare bones, 
and then lets them on their way. Remove all modifications, cargo, 
passengers, and crew from the captain's starship. All passengers 
and crew are sold into slavery. The number of crew and passen-
gers you remove are added to the Compensation section on the 
log sheet as compensation must be paid for them.
If the captain has no modifications, cargo, passengers, or crew 
onboard at the start of this event, the Arrengale take the cap-
tain's starship from them and sell the captain into slavery, see

The judge reads out your sentence and you're condemned to spend 
the rest of your life frozen, in a Cryo-Prison. You was hoping for 
trial by combat. However, this punishment is a small consolation 
to being put to death. The security droids march you to a holding 
cell and from there you're transported to a Cryo-Prison. After a 
few days they process the freezing by placing you in a coffin-like 
container made of metal. You lay down inside and a droid lowers 
a lid to seal you in. In the lid is a small window, which you peer out 
of to see a droid moving around outside. You lift your head for a 
better view and see the droid bending over to press a button. You 
hear a click, but nothing happens and so it thumps it several times 
and in a tinny voice says "The cryo-chamber has a malfunction. 
The freeze pumps are stuck." It kicks the side and there is a whir-
ring noise. Then an intense pain hits your feet and rapidly spreads 
upwards into your legs, then to your waist, body and head. You 
scream out in pain and as you pass out you hear the droid say 
"Negative! Negative! The freeze pumps are now working."

ing off the freeze pumps. Every so often when the chamber de-
activates it gives the captain a chance of escape.

Cyborg Attack
The history of the Cyborgs: The Biological Eradication Agency (BEA) was destroyed over a millennium ago. Its goal was to research and 
build prototype androids that could detect and eliminate micro-organisms causing sickness and disease throughout the galaxy. In a des-
perate attempt to save the company from financial ruin the BEA replaced factory workers with droids at a number of its facilities. A decade 
later and profits were up; the directors seized the opportunity to make more money and replaced their engineers and scientists with cyborg 
research units. These research bots were programmed to program and develop new eliminator bots. Soon the Assassinator model, the 
Enforcer model, and the Destroyer model were flooding the market and the directors were swimming in credits. The units were advertised 
to not only eliminate micro threats but could also be used to run security details, enforce crowd control, police star ports and even used as 
cyber soldiers during a war. Then, due to the cyber wars in the last millennium, it all went wrong for the BEA. Millions and millions of cyborg 
soldiers were being built every month so rival corporations and governments could go to war without suffering any loss of biological life. 
However the research bots and droids at the factories didn’t see it this way; to them millions of their own kind were being slaughtered so 
the “Bios” (the name given to the biological beings) could live without consequence. They rose up and eliminated the directors, and began 
a strategy to gain domination over all biological life forms across the galaxy. They now build themselves and have become a recognised 
race by the Galactic Defence League (GDL). They are a scourge to all biological life forms, whom they seek to destroy and will kill on sight. 
As well as a huge army of cyborg soldiers, they have built thousands of starships to move troops around the galaxy. They will attack any 
starship they come across, whenever their scanners show it has biological life onboard.
A very large starship appears on the long range proximity scanner warning you of an intercept. It has no life signs onboard and no 
authorised security signatures. It has no business to approach your starship. You program a few evasive manoeuvre into the navigation 
computer, but the ship compensates to maintain an intercept. As the ship comes in to view your heart sinks, it is a cyborb vessel. You feel 
sick to the stomach and expect the worst. Desperately you try to engage the jump drive, but the cyborg vessel is using a disruptor and 
the signal is scrambling your controls. You stare out at the ship trying to think of something to do, and then several lights flash across 
the open space from the cyborg ship to yours. You're too late, they are onboard!
The cyborg have boarded the captain's starship and are now in 
the process of eliminating any crew, and passenger onboard; 
as well as the captain. Roll 2d10 on the Cyborg Chart (on the 
right) to determine the cyborg the captain is confronted with 
and begin combat. The cyborg attacking the captain will never 
try to escape combat and all results it makes on the reaction 
table that would result in it escaping are ignored.
Each Security crew member onboard will fight alongside the 
captain. Therefore, each group of 5 Security crew members (or 
part of) gives the captain +10 to their attack characteristic (ei-
ther Str, Dex, or Int) and +2 damage bonus.
Example: If there are 1-5 Security crew onboard, the captain 
gains +10 to their attack characteristic and +2 Dmg. If there are 
6-10 Security crew onboard, the captain gains +20 to their at-
tack characteristic and +4 Dmg.
During the combat with the captain other cyborgs all around 
the ship are killing the crew and passengers. At the start of each 
combat round roll 1d3. This is the number of crew or passengers 
that have been killed by the cyborg. Choose which passengers, or 
crew members are killed from the log sheet and remove them. 
Don't forget to add the number that are killed to the compensa-
tion box. If you cannot remove a passenger or a crew member 
from the log sheet, because none remain, each crew member 
or passenger that you cannot remove is instead converted into a 
+10 AV, and a +1 Dmg modifier that is applied to the cyborg the 
captain is fighting for the forthcoming combat round.
Example: Jacob rolls a 3 for the cyborg's attack on the passengers 
and crew, but only has 1 passenger remaining and no crew. He 
removed the last passenger from the log sheet and the cyborg 
gains +20 AV and +2 Dmg modifier during the next combat round. 
When the combat with the captain is over, so is the cyborg at-
tack on the ship and you can continue with the game.

Game Over
Your body has given up and your brain function diminishes.
You have been directed here because your captain has perished. 
What happens now? Well you have a two options as follows:
You can continue playing with a new captain in the same galaxy your 
departed captain was exploring. To do this, create a new captain 
in the usual way, but skip the Creating A New Galaxy section. In-
stead, choose any one of the hex sheets your departed captain had 
explored and roll for a random star system; this is the star system 
where your new captain will begin (docked at its space port). If the 
star system hasn't yet been generated, you must generate it. All hex 
sheets, star system and zone sheets, and economy sheets created 
for the galaxy are used by the new captain. The departed captain's 
Star Date Chart is then refreshed; you remove all shaded days and 
trigger arrows g that were on the Star Date Chart and place a line 
through all date entries made on the reverse, they are now void and 
no longer apply. Then remove all shaded pips from the Action Point 
Tracker. You are now ready to begin playing from where your depart-
ed captain left off. However, is your new captain a beneficiary of the 
departed captain's estate? You can make this as a personal choice, if 
you choose yes then see the Beneficiary event.
Alternatively, you can play with a new captain in a different galaxy 
to the one your departed captain was exploring. To do this, simply 
create a new captain and begin the section Creating A New Galaxy.

Malaria
You begin to feel very ill, and are suffering from a very high fever. 
You are shaking all over, and can’t get warm no matter what you 
try. Your head is pounding with a terrible headache and you have 
terrible pain in your muscles and joints. As well being exhausted 
all the time, you are nauseous and constantly vomiting. You have 
terrible diarrhoea each time you eat and drink, and areas of your 
skin and the whites of your eyes have become yellow with anae-
mia and jaundice. You spend the next few weeks trying to recover.
Mark off 1d3 +1 weeks on the star chart, and reduce the captain's 
HP to 1. Next, perform the RECOVERY test below. If the test fails, 
you may spend a life point and turn the result into a success.
RECOVERY – Test: Str -15 [S: -10 Primary STR] [F: Death, see the 
Game Over event] (Strong)

Message
The communications sensors are picking up a strange message. It 
appears coded, but could be an alien language. After a short while 
a translation of the message pops up on the screen.
See the Rumour event.
Message Sent
A few moments later after sending the message a man in his thir-
ties pops up on your communication screen. He is starting to go 
grey and speaks with a strange accent. Cybercon™ wires are pro-
truding from his head.
"Hello, I am Dr Gurcar Neapman, I have been expecting you; I have 
read through your medical records. Very interesting case indeed. 
I would like you to shuttle over so we can help you." You leave im-
mediately and when you arrive you spot some worker droids, but 
no life forms. You stand for a while and one approaches. It is a ser-
vice droid. You notice a blaster hole through one of its wheels. The 
damage is causing the droid to spin left, whilst the other wheels 
are straining to keep it moving forwards. 
"Good DAY to YOUUuuhiss. I wiLL Be youRrrhiss healTH aSSistan-
thiss TOoodDay. PleeAASSE FolloWwhiss MeeeE." The droids 
speech is way off and in need of a good calibration. Its volume is 
up and down and some words trails off into a static hiss. You fol-
low the droid down a long windowless corridor to a small white 
room. At the centre is a white metal bed with a flat white pillow. 
A retractable light is flickering on and off above the bed. Around 
the room are several low level cupboards with metal worktops 
laid out with various medical equipment; mostly scanners, me-
chanical forceps, and laser knives, but there are a few primitive 
surgeon tools and plenty of metal dishes and suction hoses. Near 
the door is a trolley loaded with 2 waist high canisters. Digital 
regulators are fixed to the top. On the bed is a data pad with 
a questionnaire which the droid instructs you to fill out. It's a 
typical consent form for surgery. When you’ve finished, the droid 
takes the pad and turns awkwardly on its damaged wheel and 
makes for the door.
"PleeAASSE laAayhiis onhiss thEe BEDddhiss Annd YoUUUur sur-
geon wiLL Be with YOUUuuhiss shortlyeehiss." The droid stops at 
the canisters and presses a button; you hear a faint beep and then 
it continues through the door. Something does not seem quite 
right and you have a bad feeling. When you walk to the door it 
shuts. There is no switch, or button on the inside. You hear another 
beep and one of the canisters jolts, then gas escapes from its regu-
lator. A moment later, the other canister jolts too and gas escapes. 
They mix in the air and a blue fog fills the room. Holding your 
breath, you keep as low as possible looking for a way to escape. 
You reach the bed and trip, and land on the floor. You're struggling 
to hold your breath but the fall causes you to take in a breath and 
immediately you pass out.
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event and 
delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer applies. 
Remove the AMF from the zone.
Next, look at your Law value. If it is 1 or below see the Surgery 
event. If it is 2 or higher see the Old Age event.
Metal Deposits
On the way to the starship you scan the area and pick up a large 
area of metal deposits a few miles away from your current loca-
tion. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and fly over to 
investigate and find the area was once a metal refinery, but only a 
few months ago went out of business. The site is completely emp-
ty apart from several containers filled with metal deposits.
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking 
what’s already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to de-
termine how many units of metal you may add to the ship's car-
go hold (space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANS-
FER CARGO test below as many times as you like to transfer as 
much, or as little of the cargo you like to the captain's ship.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)

Mission
You're relaxing in one of the many bars enjoying a drink when 
a guy on the next table tells an amazing story to his friend. It 
appears to be about a job that he is going to do sometime soon 
and he's asking his friend if he would like to go with him and split 
the reward. You lean closer, but he notices and begins talking in 
whispers. He obviously doesn't want to share any details of the 
job with anyone else.
-1 AP. If you wish you may perform the EAVESDROP test below 
to see if the captain can find out what the job entails and dis-
cover how to get involved. If the test is a successful the captain 
has learnt details of a mission, see Generating Operations. If the 
test is failed, the guy and his friend move to another table, be-
cause they have become aware of the captain's eavesdropping; 
and the captain learns nothing.
EAVESDROP - Test: Int -20 [S: You hear everything] [F: They no-
tice you and move to another table] (Aware)

Mistaken Mutant
"MUTANT! Its a mutant". You start to run and they give 
chase. Glancing over your shoulder you see a mob has 
formed and they are gaining on you. Laser bolts whistle 
past your ear. They have opened fire!
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from 
the star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
It doesn't matter if the captain is a mutant or not, you must 
perform the following:
The captain must escape the mob, or be killed. Perform 
the ESCAPE MOB test below until the captain has escaped 
4 mobs or their HP has been reduced to 0 or less (in which 
case they have been killed). Note: whilst escaping the cap-
tain may not perform any action to restore lost HP. If the 
captain is killed see the Game Over event; however, spend-
ing a life point will prevent the captain's death and end this 
event; the captain will have escaped the mob.
ESCAPE MOB – Test: Dex -10 [S: Escaped from 1 mob] [F: 
-1d3 HP] (Escape)

Mutant
Centuries ago in a distant galaxy, a biowarfare laboratory created 
a disease to infect and mutate DNA. The disease was so highly 
contagious it spread across space like a wildfire. In an effort to 
get it under control, a Kill Mutants On Sight (KMOS) policy was 
introduced. Now two thousand years on and it is extremely rare to 
discover a mutant, but every so often sightings are reported and 
when they are special forces are activated to hunt them down and 
exterminate them. 
There isn’t a known cure for those infected with the disease, but a 
few optimistic mutants speculate that somewhere in the laboratory 
where the disease was developed, is the bio-coding needed to pro-
duce a cure. However, the biowarfare laboratory has never been 
discovered and its whereabouts is now lost in time.
If the captain already has the Mutant disease, you need do nothing 
further and can continue with the game, otherwise please read on.
Unfortunately, the captain has been in contact with a mutant and 
now fears they have the disease. Roll 1d100-30, if the result is 
equal to or less than the captain's primary HP they have man-
aged to avoid the disease and you may continue with the game; 
otherwise, the captain has contracted the Mutant disease and 
must shade the star date 1d10+20 days in the future. Then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and 
something does not feel right. See the Mutated event." 

Mutated
This morning when you awoke you felt strange and it suddenly be-
came apparent; the mutant you encountered a few weeks ago has 
infected you with the mutant disease and a mutation has surfaced.
The captain is now a mutant, there is no known cure. Near the 
top of the new style log sheet is a Mutant box. Shade the box to 
signify the captain is now a mutant 
The captain will need to be very careful or run the risk of being 
discovered as a mutant. The penalty is immediate death. Next 
to the Mutant box is a DV box where you will record the cap-
tain's Discovery Value, the higher this value the more chance 
there is the captain will be discovered. On the reverse of the log 
sheet is a section called "Mutations", this is where you record 
the mutations and any special rules they have; there is space for 
four mutations (the maximum). The following rules now apply 
for the mutated captain. 
When you're first directed to this event complete step 1 and gen-
erate the captain's first mutation.
1.	
Mutations: Each time the captain is instructed to gain a 
mutation follow the instructions below:
1.	
Roll 1d00 on the Mutation Chart (see below) and add 
the mutation to the Mutations section on the reverse 
of the log sheet. Note: A mutation will only manifest 
itself once, if you generate a mutation the captain al-
ready has, ignore the result and roll again for another. 
2.	
Add 5 to the captain's Discovery Value (DV).
3.	
If the captain now has four mutations ignore this step, 
otherwise shade the star date 1d10+90 days in the fu-
ture, and make the following date entry: "[DATE] You 
awake in the morning and something does not feel 
right. See the Mutated event and generate another 
mutation (step 1)." 
2.	
The Cure: Whenever the captain begins an away mission, 
there is a chance that somewhere on the mission the captain 
may come across the bio-coding needed to produce a cure. 
The chances are extremely low; however, before the mission 
roll 1d100; on a result of 100 it's possible the captain may find 
the bio-coding in the form of an Objective Item. The first ob-
jective item you add to the log sheet whilst on the mission is 
the bio-coding. Next, the captain must find a batch of chemi-
cals to be loaded into a special bio-chamber. This is where the 
captain will lay and be injected with the chemicals. Therefore, 
the second Objective Item added to the log sheet is the batch 
of chemicals. When the two Objective Items (The bio-coding 
and the batch of chemicals) have been added to the log sheet, 
the captain must then find the bio-chamber. Each green area 
you add to the map sheet from this point on, roll 1d6. On a 
result of a 1 or a 6 do not roll for its geographic feature, in-
stead it contains the bio-chamber. Remove the two objective 
items from the log sheet and then remove all mutations from 
the log sheet and the shading from the mutant box. The cap-
tain is no longer a Mutant and has been cured. Note: When a 
mutation is removed, if it made an adjustment to a primary 
characteristic (i.e. BIG HEAD, TRIPLE JOINTED, BIG ARMS etc.) 
the adjustment must be reversed. 
3.	
Port Phase: The following rules apply when the captain is at 
a Space Station 
 or a Military Dock 
 :
The captain will modify their appearance and adjust equip-
ment in order to try and hide their mutations; this occurs 
automatically and you do not need to keep track, but you 
do need to determine if the captain will be discovered whist 
performing port activities. 
The general public may spot the mutation and alert the 
authorities, or the port may have Mutant Hunters on the 
look out for potential targets. Mutant Hunters will kill on 
sight and ask questions later. Therefore, at the start of any 
port phase after the docking phase has been completed 
you must perform one of the DISCOVERY test below. Which 
one is determined by the type of port the captain is dock 
at. The test is modified by the captain's current Discovery 
Value (DV), and so the more mutations the captain has, the 
harder it will be for them to remain undiscovered.
Also, if the port is marked with "(MPOI)" after its name on 
the Star Systems & Zones sheet, you must add +10 to the 
d100 roll when you make the test. This is because the cap-
tain has previously been identified at the port for being a 
mutant and the port authorities are on the look out for an-
yone matching their description. 
If the test is passed successfully you may continue the port 
phase as normal; otherwise, the captain has at some time 
during the port phase been identified as a mutant, see the 
Discovered event.
DISCOVERY 
 – Test: Int -DV [S: Continue with the port 
phase as normal] [F: Captain is identified as a mutant, see 
Discovered event] (Aware)
DISCOVERY 
 – Test: Int -10, -DV [S: Continue with the 
port phase as normal] [F: Captain is identified as a mutant, 
see Discovered event] (Aware)

Narcotics Stash
The long range scanners alert you to a strange magnetic iron pattern 
around a small asteroid field. You change course to investigate and 
when you reach the asteroid field you find it is in fact a cluster of 
crates floating in space. The magnetic iron pattern is caused by a high 
tech plasma net that is holding the crates in a group and preventing 
them from floating away. You scan a crate and manage to bypass the 
interference caused by the net and find that it is filled with narcotics.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of narcotics you 
may add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you 
may perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the 
cargo to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as 
little of the cargo you like that is available. If you take any of the 
narcotics gain +1 Law.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
New Habit
After the away mission you feel alive, full of energy, and hyped up. 
You can't help wondering if the space dust you took has somehow 
chemically imbalanced your body and mind. After a while the ef-
fects wear off and you feel a little out of it and vulnerable.
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event and 
delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer applies. 
If the captain already has a value recorded in the Habit section 
on the log sheet, this event comes to an end; otherwise read on.
Add 9 to the Habit section on the log sheet. The captain now has 
a craving to use more space dust. Each time the captain begin an 
away mission you must roll 1d100. If the result is equal to or less 
than the captain's current habit value, the captain must immedi-
ately use a space dust item on the log sheet. If the captain does 
not have any space dust items on the log sheet they suffer -10 Str, 
-10 Dex, and -10 Int for the entire Away Mission. A reminder of 
this is also shown on the log sheet in the Habit section.
Now that the captain has a mild habit forming. They may feel 
the need to visit a space dust seller from time to time. There-
fore during a port phase, if the captain's habit value is 1 or more 
they may seek out a space dust seller, and you refer to the Deal-
er Of Space Dust event. A reminder of this is also shown on the 
log sheet in the Habit section.
If at anytime the captain's habit value is ever reduced to 0 they 
no longer have a habit and no longer need to check if they need 
to have any space dust before an away mission.
Nomads
On the way back to the starship you spot a group of figures moving 
towards you in the distance. Your scanner doesn’t pick up any weap-
on signatures and so you're fairly certain they are unarmed. When 
you're closer, they are friendly and ask you to join them at their 
camp a few miles away. Luckily it's in the direction you're heading 
towards your starship. They're nomads and appear to be from a 
low tech civilization. You pull a cloak over yourself to hide as much 
of your equipment as you can. At the camp you're ushered through 
a powered doorway into a stone complex, much like a fortification. 
The place is a city rather than a mere camp with hundreds of peo-
ple going about their business. Your translator must have struggled 
to interpret their word for city and came up with camp, unless of 
course the nomads lied. You begin to feel quite nervous and start to 
worry, if this has been a huge mistake!
-1d3 AP. Roll 1d6 to see what happens at the nomad city.
1.	
The captain is taken a prison camp within the city and is 
judged for a crime they neither understand or committed; 
see the Sold Into Slavery event.
2.	
The captain is robbed and then thrown out of the city, see 
the Robbed event.
3.	
The captain is treated suspiciously by the other nomads 
and is attacked by a mob and beaten (-1d10 HP). If the cap-
tain survives the beating, they are thrown out of the city 
and left for dead. The captain makes it back to the ship.
4.	
The nomads want to share food and water and some stories. 
The captain gains 1d3 rations and picks up a rumour; see the 
Rumour event.
5.	
The nomads want to sell the captain 1d6 goods they have 
acquired. For each good they have for sale, choose one of 
the following tables: Table A, K, N, TA, or W. Then roll on the 
chosen table to see what is being offered for sale. The cap-
tain is free to buy any or none of the items that are offered.
6.	
The nomads are healers and want to heal the captain's 
wounds; restore all lost HP. If the captain didn't have any 
wounds to heal (i.e. HP is at maximum), they instead offer 
the captain the following item which you may add to the 
log sheet: (XL) MED PACK: Use to replenish up to 10 lost HP. 
The Med Pack is worth 200c.

Old Age
You wake after passing out and find yourself in a white room, in a 
bed, and with the man you saw on your communications screen. 
He is looking down at you.
"It didn't go well I'm afraid. We tried to buy you some time; but it's 
old age catching up with you I am afraid. Nothing can be done" 
You thank the doctor for trying and are relieved to find out that 
the surgery was funded by a research program he is involved with, 
so no charge. You spend some days in recovery and are transport-
ed back to your ship. 
Mark off 1d3+6 days on the Star Date Chart. 
On The Look Out
You reduce speed and listen out for the docking anchors to latch 
onto the ship. You hear the clanking sound and count four. With 
the ship safely docked you head for the airlock and step out onto 
the platform. As you pass other vessels, you keep an eye out for 
your old ship. It was stolen a short while ago and you hope one 
day to see it again. 
To determine if you find your stolen ship follow the instructions 
below.
Note: If the captain's starship is returned to the captain, it has 
been stripped of all modifications and there is no cargo on-
board. For reference: the captain's old starship's model type 
can be found in the date entry which triggered this event. 
1.	
Count the number of days that have elapsed since the theft. 
This will be from the date marked with the trigger arrow g 
that triggered this event. If the result is 99, or less go to 
step 2. If the result is 100 or higher, your ship is long gone 
and will never be seen again; well by you at least. Place a 
line through the date entry that triggered this event and 
delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer 
applies; then, end this event and continue with the game.
2.	
Roll the 1d100; if the result is equal to, or more than the 
number of days that have expired, the captain spots their 
old starship, go to step 3; however, if the result is lower the 
ship is nowhere to be seen and this event comes to an end.
3.	
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event 
and delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no 
longer applies. Next choose 1 of the 4 options below.
a.	
Do nothing and let the theft go unanswered.
b.	 Contact the port's authorities with the details of the 
theft of the starship. See the Report event. If the crim-
inal is punished the starship is returned to the captain.
c.	
Confront the thieves. Shade 1d10 Action Pips (AP). 
This is the time it takes for the thieves to return to the 
stolen starship. Then see the Confront event.
d.	 Steal back the starship. See the Stealing A Starship 
event. If the event is successful the captain steals back 
their ship.

Rifter
Rifters are an ancient order going back six millennia. They use 
mind control and telekinesis to perform all kinds of strange and 
mystical effects. The Rifter Program was created in the last cen-
tury and outlaws the use of Rifter "Wizardly" in all but a few star 
systems. Wherever the program is upheld, the Rifters have moved 
underground and are still practicing their powers.
Every life form in the galaxy is built upon an energy that keeps them 
alive. Those that have unlocked the secrets of this energy and can 
use it for wondrous effects are known as Rifters. The captain has 
been given an insight into the power of the Rifters and must now 
decide if they will embrace the Rifter way of life, or not. If the cap-
tain decides to be a Rifter there is no turning back; and all of the 
following rules will apply for the duration of the captain's life; so 
please read through them carefully before making a decision.
1.	
Shade the Rifter box (found on the front of the new log sheet 
under the tracks section) to activate the Rifter rules. This sig-
nifies the captain is now a Rifter. 
2.	
Shade the box on the Rifter skill (found where the experi-
ence star is usually located). it's now active and can be used. 
There isn’t a skill bonus yet, but one can be gained through 
using its experience track (just like the other skills).
3.	
Rifters are generally frowned upon by law enforcers. They 
have a tendency to speak out against the law and politics 
and are known to interfere in the affairs of governments 
and star systems. Therefore, as a Rifter the captain will al-
ways have a minimum Law value of 1, and a maximum Rep 
value of 9. If necessary make the adjustments to Law and 
Rep to conform to these restraints.
4.	
As a result of manipulating their inner power, most Rifters 
adopt a natural yearning to help out and assist, especially 
those in less fortunate situations. For this reason a Rifter 
captain must always tackle an Instant Mission when one 
is available, and they are not permitted to take the fail op-
tion. In addition, each time the captain docks at a Space 
Station 
, before they take any port activities they must 
spend 1 hour (-1AP) visiting the homeless shelters at the 
port; where they hand out some credits to those in need 
(-100c). If the captain has insufficient credits record them 
as a negative value; however, by the end of the port phase 
the captain must have 0 credits or more, even if it means 
they have to borrow some money (see the Loan event). 
5.	
The moment the captain becomes a Rifter, they have un-
locked the first Rifter Ability. Shade the ① pip on the Rifter 
Abilities track. This means the captain may now use the first 
ability shown on the Rifter Ability Chart found on the oppo-
site page. Until others are shaded, they cannot be used.
6.	
Rifter Abilities can be used at anytime, but only when they're 
applicable. They are marked with (Combat), and (Non-Com-
bat) as a further guide. Those marked (AM) can only used 
whilst on an Away/Instant Mission. Note: Combat abilities 
do not require a combat action to use. When the captain 
uses a Rifter Ability it also cost energy and you must shade a 
number of pips equal to the ability's energy cost on the ener-
gy track, then you perform the RIFTER test below. The ener-
gy cost is shown as ⓪①②③and④. Note: If there isn't 
enough energy pips to shade, the ability cannot be used. If 
the test fails you must test the captain's energy level. 
RIFTER - Test: Int -20 [S: Ability takes effect] [F: Make an 
ENERGY TEST] (Rifter)
ENERGY TEST: Roll 1d10 and if the result is equal to or less 
than the number of pips shaded on the energy track the 
captain's energy levels are compromised (-1d3 HP). 
7.	
If you make a RIFTER test and score a natural roll of 10 or less, 
you may either shade 2 pips on the Rifter skill's experience 
track, shade 1 pip on the Int experience track, or replenish 1d3 
power (i.e. remove shaded pips equal to the number rolled). 
However, if you score a natural 5 or less, you may perform 
one of the above options, or alternatively roll for a new Rifter 
Ability. To roll for a new Rifter Ability, roll 1d10 on the Rifter 
Abilities Chart and if the ability rolled is not already shaded on 
the log sheet you gain that ability and can go ahead and shade 
it. However if you generate an ability the captain already has 
acquired, no new Rifter Ability is gained on this occasion.
8.	
Energy is naturally replenished each time a day is checked off 
on the Star Date Chart at the rate of 1 energy per day. There-
fore, each day the captain spends on an away mission (show-
ing ⊞ on the Star Date Chart) or checks off on the Star Date 
Chart replenishes 1 energy (i.e. 1 shaded pip is removed).

Slavery
The judge reads out your sentence and you're condemned to 
spend the rest of your life in slavery. You was hoping for Incarcer-
ation. However, you know the punishment is far better than facing 
a trial by combat. The security droids holding you, march you to a 
holding cell and from there you're transported to a slave ship. You 
have no idea where they have taken you, but after processing you 
find yourself working in a slave mine. Day after day you're taken 
to a small moon to extract minerals in an underground quarry.

escaping and hope one day your dream will come true!
Add 1d6+6 years to the Star Year box on the Star Date Chart. 
This is the number of years that have passed before an escape 
attempt can be made. For each year you add, you must apply 
the Aging modifier, which could end up triggering the Time Is 
Almost Up event. Note: If the Time Is Almost Up event is trig-
gered, or if you already have the following entry on the reverse 
of the time sheet: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and are 
feeling terrible. See the Life Expectancy event."; unfortunately 
the captain has died of old age, see the Game Over event. Any 
trigger arrows g, or other shaded dates remain in place, but do 
not activate them or deal with them. 
If the captain survives this time period of slavery reduce their 
Law to 6 and deduct -4 Rep; they can now begin trying to es-
cape captivity by performing an ESCAPE SLAVERY test each year. 
The test is made using the captain's primary Dex value with a 
-10 modifier. When performing the test, none of the captain's 
items can be used (as they have been taken from them), nor can 
any Cybercon™ implants (as they have been deactivated). Begin 
by performing the test below.
ESCAPE SLAVERY - Test: Primary Dex -10 [S: Freed] [F: Add 1 
year to the Star Year box.] (Escape)
If the test is passed successfully the captain has found a way 
to escape and has managed to reach a port in a random star 
system. Roll for a random star system. If the star system is not 
yet generated, you must generate it. The captain continues the 
game from the port in the star system. They have no posses-
sions or a starship, remove all of the following from the log 
sheet: Credits, Armour, Weapons, items in the Utility Belt, Ox-
ygen O2, Night Vision, Rations, Decoders, Power Cells, all Items 
in the Large and Small equipment packs, and the Starship from 
the log sheet. The captain does however, manage to reactivate 
their Cybercon™ implants. Next, add a trigger arrow g to the 
current star date and make the following date entry:"[DATE] 
The captain is an escaped slave from the [SYSTEM] system. 
When in zone 1 of the [SYSTEM] system, see the Tracked Down 
event." Note: You replaced [SYSTEM] with the name of the star 
system the captain suffered the Judged event in. The captain's 
only choice is to borrow some credits. See the Loan event.
If the test fails, for the next year the captain is placed in a gang 
of workers that are prone to trying to escape. Extra security is 
placed on this gang to watch for escape attempts. You then add 
1 year to the Star Year box and perform the test again.
Note: Each year until the captain has escaped you must apply the 
Aging modifier; and if the Time Is Almost Up event is triggered 
the captain has died, see the Game Over event.

tain to pay out compensation. Total up the compensation 
costs (see Compensation/Escape Pod# on page 14) from 
the Passenger Manifest and Crew section on the log sheet, 
and remove the credits. Then remove the crew and passen-
gers from the log sheet.
4.	
Next, add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and 
make the following date entry:"[DATE] Your starship, a 
[MODEL] was stolen and you're now on the look out for 
the thieves. When you dock at a space port see the On the 
Look Out event." Replace the word [MODEL] with the mod-
el of the captain's starship.
5.	
You may now begin the port phase. It would be a good idea 
to buy a new ship. If you lack the funds you may acquire a 
loan, see the Loan event.
Storm
On the way back to the starship a terrifying geomagnetic storm 
erupts and you're forced to take shelter. After a few hours you be-
lieve you can press on in relative safety.
Test STORM below. If you pass the test successfully the captain 
has reached the shuttle that will take them to the starship. If the 
test fails you must test again and continue to perform the test 
until it is either passed successfully, or you have failed the test 
4 times. On the 4th failed test, the captain has managed to find 
their way to the shuttle which will fly them to the starship.
STORM – Test: Str -15 [S: -1d3 AP, -1d3 HP, reached shuttle] [F: -1 
d3 AP, -1d3 HP] (Strong)
Stop And Search
A large starship drops out of warp directly beside your ship. It's the 
star system's stop and search patrol. An automated voice comes 
through the communication channel "This is a routine stop and 
search. You are obliged by galactic law to lower your shields and 
allow a patrol crew to board your vessel. Non-compliance and we 
have the authority to gain access to your ship by force." 
If the captain does not wish to be boarded, they will have to 
fight the stop and search patrol ship, roll 1d10+90 on table S 
- Starships to see which starship the captain will face and then 
decide if they will attack or not. If they attack, conduct a space 
combat with the stop and search patrol ship.
If the captain does not fight the patrol ship, they have no choice 
but to lower the shields and allow a droid patrol onboard. 
If the there is any Contraband, Narcotics, or Weapons onboard 
the ship the captain must perform the SMUGGLE test below. If 
the test is failed, the illegal cargo is discovered and the stop and 
search patrol beams them and the captain back to their ship for 
an arrest, see ARRESTED below.
SMUGGLE - Test: Int [S: Cargo remains hidden] [F: Cargo is dis-
covered, +1 Law, -1000c, all red goods are removed, see AR-
RESTED below] (Aware, Smuggler)
If the captain passes the SMUGGLE test, or didn't have any con-
traband, Narcotics or Weapons onboard. The captain may be 
identified as a wanted fugitive, see below. 
If the captain's Law value is 0 or less, they are not wanted by the 
authorities and have nothing to fear from the stop and search; 
the event is now over. However, if the captain's Law value is 
1 or more, roll 1d10. If the result is equal to or less than the 
captain's law value, they have been rumbled and the stop and 
search patrol beams them and the captain back to their ship for 
an arrest, see ARRESTED below.
ARRESTED: The captain is placed in cuffs and transported back 
to the nearest port to be processed. Change the captain's posi-
tion to the closest zone containing a port point of interest, then 
see the Judged event.
Stranger
Welcome aboard stranger! The stranger joins the crew and also 
becomes a close friend.
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
You've made friends with a stranger, and for a while they spend 
some time onboard your starship. 
Shade the star date 1d10+20 days in the future. Then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] A stranger you welcomed on-
board your starship is about to disembark, they have become a 
dear friend whilst onboard, see the Disembark event."

Surgery
You wake after passing out and find yourself in a white room, in a 
bed, and with the man you saw on your communications screen. He 
is looking down at you."It all went well and we have bought you some 
time. Time is all we can offer, not a cure. It's age catching up with you 
I am afraid." You thank the doctor and are pleased to find out that 
the surgery has been funded by a research program. You spend some 
days in recovery and are then transported back to your ship. 
Change the captain's maximum primary HP value to 19. Then, 
mark off 1d3+6 days on the Star Date Chart. 
Surrender
You surrender peacefully and they beam you aboard their ship. 
You are stripped of everything you own and sold into slavery.
See the Sold Into Slavery event.
Tech Ship
The long range scanners alert you to a starship floating in 
space. It's heavily damaged and all of its escape pods have been 
launched. You perform a deep scan and it shows there are no life 
signs onboard, but it's carrying a large quantity of tech goods. 
You change course to intercept and find the ship has been blown 
in two. Some of the tech crates are floating around the wreck and 
are just waiting to be scooped up. 
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of tech goods you 
may add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you 
may perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the 
cargo to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as 
little of the cargo you like that is available.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Textile Crates
The long range scanners alert you to a high radiation signal in 
an area of space not usually frequented by starships. You change 
course to investigate. When you reach the signal, you see the 
cause immediately; a solar flare from the system's star has caused 
a solar magnetic storm. Unfortunately a starship must have got 
itself caught in the coronal mass ejection and its crew have been 
wiped out from exposure to the high levels of radiation. The ship's 
computer system is fried and nothing is working. A scan of the 
cargo hold reveals a large number of crates filled with textiles. You 
scan for radiation onboard the ship and it registers a slow dilution 
within the surrounding atmosphere; currently the radiation level 
is just below safety protocols and it's safe to transport the cargo.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of textiles you may 
add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you may 
perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the cargo 
to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as little of 
the cargo you like that is available.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Time Is Almost Up
Getting old isn't so great. You can feel everything straining. Mus-
cle aches, stiff back, poor eye sight, and strained hearing; are the 
least of your worries. Today you felt something more than just 
getting old; the pain was deeper and it won't go away. You get up 
and dress and then jump into the ship's medical booth. It shows 
some strange readings and across the screen flashing in red is the 
message "Emergency: Report to a Doctor!"
You no longer roll 2d10 when you apply the yearly modifier to 
your primary maximum values. Make a note at the top of the log 
sheet "Ignore 2d10 yearly modifier check" as a reminder. 
Next, shade the star date 1d10+20 days in the future. Then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and 
are feeling terrible. See the Life Expectancy event." 
Next, add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and then 
make the following date entry:"[DATE] If you visit a medic during 
a Medic activity, see the Fighting Back event."
Tracked Down
You try to blend in and remain hidden, but your ship is spotted, and 
a starship moves in to intercept. The starship is making very precise 
tactical manoeuvres to block your escape. Over the communica-
tions a voice says "Captain you have been identified as a person of 
interest who has the classification of "Wanted". Please lower your 
shields and allow us to transport over to deal with your surrender."
Roll on table S - Starships and apply the current star system's 
threat level modifier. This is the starship that has tracked down 
the captain and is blocking their escape.
You have a few choices to choose from, see below. You may per-
form them as many times as you wish, and even choose differ-
ent options until you either escape the enemy starship, defeat 
it in space combat, or surrender.
1.	
Jump To Another Star System: If you choose this option, se-
lect a  jump lane and perform the modified JUMP test below. 
The test is handled like any other jump test; except, if the test 
is successful the captain has outmanoeuvred the enemy star-
ship and has managed to escape. The captain is then required 
to reach the chosen stars system, by making standard jump 
tests. If the test is failed, the enemy starship has managed to 
fire at the captain's starship and aborted the jump test; you 
may if you wish try again, or choose another option.
JUMP - Test: Int +/- CM, -30 [S: -1 PL, travels, - fuel, escape, 
gain 1 Law] [F: -1d6+6 PL] (Navigators) 
2.	
Move To Adjacent Zone: If you choose this option perform 
the modified SPACE CRUISE test below. 
SPACE CRUISE - Test: Int +/- CM, -20 [S: -1 PL, move to adja-
cent zone, test HIDE AND SEEK] [F: -1d6+6 PL] (Pilots)
If the test is successful the captain has outmanoeuvred the 
enemy starship and has moved to an adjacent zone; howev-
er, you must then test HIDE AND SEEK to see if it manages to 
follow and find the captain's starship in the adjacent zone. 
HIDE AND SEEK - Test: Int +/- CM, -20 [S: Escaped, +1 Law] 
[F: -1d6+6 PL] (Pilots)

"[DATE] Each time the captain docks at a space port roll 1d6, 
on a result of 1 or 6 the Transcendental Alien's prediction were

Until the captain has escaped the enemy starship, they may 
not interact with any points of interest in either zone. If ei-
ther the SPACE CRUISE, or the HIDE AND SEEK test fails, the 
enemy starship has fired and hit the captain's starship and

3.	
Surrender: If you choose this option, the shields are low-
ered and a boarding party arrives and transports the cap-
tain to the nearest space port, the captain is now in the 
system's zone that has the Space Station, or Military Dock. 
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event 
and delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no 
longer applies. Then, see the Law event.
4.	
Attack: If you choose this option gain +1 Law, then begin 
a space combat with the enemy starship (you can find its 
details on table S - Starships). The captain may not choose 
Evasive Manoeuvres in the first combat round. Then:
A.	 If the captain, or the enemy escapes, the event is over.
B.	 If the enemy starship has 0 LS (because it's destroyed or 
captured) gain +1 Law and the event is over. Note: If the 
captain's starship is stolen (i.e. has a SSD number after 
its name) and the captain was trying to dock at a port, 
they must immediately leave the zone and may not re-
attempt to dock at the space port for at least another 
thirty days; add a trigger arrow g to the current star 
date and then make the following date entry: "[DATE] 
The captain must not dock at [PORT] in the [SYSTEM] 
system until after [EXPIRE DATE]." Replace the [EXPIRE 
DATE] with the date 30 days in the future. Note: The 
captain is free to fly in and out of the zone, but just can-
not dock at the port until the 30 days has expired.
C.	
If the captain's starship has 0 LS (because it's destroyed 
or captured), the captain is transported to the enemy 
starship and forced to surrender. The captain is then tak-
en to the star system's zone that has a port. Place a line 
through the date entry that triggered this event and de-
lete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer 
applies. Then, see the Law event. Note: the captain does 
not receive any insurance money for their captured or 
destroyed starship and so if the captain lacks the funds 
to purchase a new starship after the Law event has esca-
lated to a punishment from a Judged event, they must 
borrow the money in order to continue with the game, 
see the Loan event at the appropriate time.
Transcendental Alien
You feel sublime. You turn to face a wondrous being. Tentacles 
float forward from its head, and when it speaks you hear the 
words in your thoughts. The alien is using telepathy and asks 
you to stay a while. You're unable to refuse and stand in a trance 
whilst it tells your future!
Add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] Each time the captain docks 
at a space port roll 1d6, on a result of 1 or 6 the Transcenden-
tal Alien's prediction were correct, [RESULT]". Roll 1d10 on the 
list below and replace [RESULT] on the date entry with the 
information rolled.

Trial By Combat
The judge reads out the sentence of Trial By Combat. You was hop-
ing to be sold into slavery. However, you know the punishment is 
far better than being place in cryo-prison for all eternity. The secu-
rity droids holding you march you to a holding cell and after a few 
hours you're taken to a large arena. 
Roll 1d10+90 on table E - Enemy from the main D100 Space rule-
book. This is the enemy the captain must now fight. Neither the 
captain or the enemy are permitted to escape combat; each re-
sult the enemy rolls on the Enemy Reaction Table that instructs 
them to escape is ignored and they instead fight as normal. The 
captain has all of the equipment that is on the log sheet at the 
time of sentencing and has been given plenty of time to re-equip 
and adjust as many items as they wish before the fight starts. 
The fight is to the death. If the captain is killed see the Game 
Over event. If the captain kills the enemy, they are released and 
you change the captain's Law value to 0 and deduct -2 Rep.
Unlawful Entry
From across the dock you spot a starship. It's a small vessel; little 
more than a shuttle. The airlock is wide open and you stroll over to 
take a peek inside. No one is around and there are no crew insight. 
You see several items that look interesting and wonder if anyone 
would notice if you went aboard to get a better look.
If the captain decides to break galactic law and enter a starship 
without the owner's/operator's consent, gain +1 Law, then see 
the Stealing event.
Velorian Fever
Velorian Fever is the most dangerous illness in all the galaxy. It is 
commonly contracted from a Velorian when they sneeze or sweat. 
The species is so toxic to all other biological life forms they have 
been banned from all non-velorian star systems, and must trav-
el in complete isolation across the galaxy. Even with these con-
straints Velorian Fever does at times breakout across the galaxy.
Whenever the captain's starship enters a star system marked 
with "VELORIAN FEVER" the star system is currently suffering 
from an outbreak of Velorian Fever; and there is a chance whilst 
in the system the captain may become infected.
When in an infected star system, each time the captain checks 
for an event (i.e. after an away mission, instant mission, space 
mission, or when playing the port phase), you must add 1d3 to 
the current "VF" number (the VF number is located in the in-
fected star system's hex on the hex sheet) and then roll 1d100. 
If you roll equal to, or less than the current VF number you must 
perform the VELORIAN FEVER test below. 
VELORIAN FEVER – Test: Int -20 [S: Not infected] [F: Contracts 
Velorian Fever, see Velorian Fever below] (Aware)
Velorian Fever: If the test fails the captain has contracted the 
Velorian Fever and suffers an illness more severe, but very sim-
ilar to Malaria; shade the star date 4d10 days in the future. 
Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A short while ago 
the captain contracted Velorian Fever, an illness very similar to 
Malaria. Deduct -1d10 primary Str, -1d10 primary Dex, -1d10 
primary Int, and -1d6 primary HP, then see the Malaria event."

Wanted Poster
Whilst walking through a busier part of port, you spot an adver-
tisement screen showing a series of wanted posters. The display 
is shuffling through quite a number of different criminals, but one 
catches your eye. You think you have seen them here in port, but 
want to check to be sure. The wanted poster eventually comes 
around again and now you're positive you have seen them and 
only just a few minutes ago!
Roll 2d10 on the Wanted Chart below to find out the crime the 
criminal is wanted for and whether they are wanted dead or 
alive. Then decide if the captain will attempt to find them. If the 
captain goes after the criminal perform the SEARCH test below. 
The SEARCH test can be made multiple times until the criminal 
is found, or the captain gives up in the attempt. If the criminal 
is found you then decide if the captain will attempt to capture 
or kill the criminal based on if the criminal is wanted dead or 
alive. If the criminal is wanted alive, you perform the ALIVE test 
below, and if the criminal is wanted dead or alive, you may per-
form either the ALIVE test below or attack them to take them 
out. The ALIVE test is modified by the Criminals Strength (CS). If 
the ALIVE test is failed, the criminal has managed to escape the 
captain and can no longer be found. If the captain attacks the 
criminal, take note of the Hostile Chart (HC) modifier and then 
see the Hostile event (use the Hostile Chart modifier in place of 
the star system's threat level when rolling on the Hostile Chart).
If the criminal is captured or killed, the captain gains the reward 
shown, but uses up 1d3 Action Pips (AP) in order to hand over the 
criminal to the authorities and fulfil the necessary paper work. 
SEARCH - Test: Int -20 [S: -1AP, criminal is found] [F: -1d3 AP, 
criminal is not found] (Aware)
ALIVE – Test: Str +/- CS [S: Criminal is captured, -1 Law] [F: -1d6+6 
HP, criminal escapes] (Strong)

War
Across the port you can hear warning sirens booming out and 
across a loud speaker you hear an announcement "WE ARE AT 
WAR!" You spot a squad of armed guards and a group of security 
droids escorting civilians towards a long line of people. The queue 
leads to the docking bay. You hear them telling everyone that the 
port is being evacuated and the consensus is to leave the star sys-
tem as soon as possible. You join the end of the line immediately.
-1d6+4 AP. Next add "AT WAR" to the star system's hex on the 
hex sheet. Add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and 
then make the following date entry: "[DATE] [SYSTEM] is at war. 
When entering [SYSTEM] roll 1d6, on a roll of 1 or 6 a ship at-
tacks, See the Ship Attacks event." Then, shade the star date

Waste Dump
The long range scanners alert you to a cluster of objects floating in 
an area of space rarely frequented these days. You change course 
to intercept and when they appear on the main display you find 
you have discovered a waste dump. Often high volumes of waste 
are dumped in quieter regions of space by waste sorting facilities, 
when they're overloaded with work. They'll usually be watched by 
security drones to stop the waste from being stolen, but on this 
occasion there are no drones keeping watch.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of waste you may 
add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you may 
perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the cargo 
to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as little

Water Mine
On the way back to the starship you scan the area. You are on the 
lookout for hostile life forms. Luckily the scanner does not pick up 
any dangers, but it does transmit data of a large cavern locat-
ed under the surface that is harbouring a vast amount of fresh 
drinking water. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and 
fly over to investigate. Built at the base of the cavern is a water 
processing plant that extracts the underground water supply, fil-
ters it and pumps it up to the surface where it's stored in large 
containers ready to be shipped. Unfortunately, a few months ago 
the plant went out of business. The site is completely empty apart 
from sealed containers filled with fresh water.
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking what’s 
already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to determine 
how many units of water you may add to the starship's cargo hold 
(space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANSFER CARGO 
test below as many times as you like to transfer as much, or as little 
of the cargo you like to the captain's ship.

Weapon Factory
On the way to the ship you scan the area and pick up a large 
quantity of weapon signatures a few miles away from your cur-
rent location. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and fly 
over to investigate and find the area was once a Weapon Factory 
that produced high-end, military grade weapons, but only a few 
months ago went out of business. The site is completely empty 
apart from sealed crates of weapons. 
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking 
what’s already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to deter-
mine how many units of weapons you may add to the ship's cargo 
hold (space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANSFER 
CARGO test below to transfer the cargo to the captain's starship.

available. If you take any of the weapons gain +1 Law.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6

Wildfire
All around, in every direction there is fire and it's spreading at 
an alarming rate. Off in the distance you see plumes of black 
smoke billowing up from the ground. You're caught in a large 
wildfire that has spread across the area for miles. You program 
your scanner for a safe route to the starship and set off. 
Test WILDFIRE below. If you pass the test successfully the captain 
has reached the shuttle that will take them to the starship. Each 
time the test fails the captain is trapped by a patch of fire and 
you must test FIRE below. After the FIRE test you must continue

captain has managed to find their way to the shuttle which will 
fly them to the starship.

FIRE – Test: Dex -10 [S: Escape fire patch safely] [F: Burnt by the 
fire, -1d3 HP] (Dodge)
