D10
Details          During an Instant Mission when you roll on table E apply the captain's current star system's threat modifier.
1 
VERMIN CONTROL [S:1d3 Rewards]
An abandoned base near to your location is overrun with vermin. The situation is causing the locals some issues 
and they have put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a c; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a c higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a c you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 4 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 4th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
BUG CONTROL [S:1d3+1 Rewards]
An abandoned base near to your location is overrun with bugs. The situation is causing the locals some issues 
and they have put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a ; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a  higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a  you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 5 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 5th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
THE CRAZY SCIENTISTS [S:1d3+2 Rewards]
A science laboratory near to your location has suffered an infestation that has caused its personnel to go crazy. The corpo-
ration running the lab has put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a t; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a t higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a t you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 6 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 6th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
THE DROID REVOLT [S:1d3+3 Rewards] O2
An industrial plant that relies solely on android staff near to your location has suffered a major insurgence over working 
conditions. The owner has put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem.
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a s; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a s higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a s you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 7 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 7th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
HALLUCINOGENIC CHEMICAL [S:1d3+4 Rewards]
A insubstantial entity has lodged itself into the air vents at an off-world military base. The creature is excreting
a hallucinogenic chemical, and the contaminated air has caused the personnel to go utterly mad. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a ≡ ; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. If 
there isn't an enemy marked with a ≡ higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies you encounter (except the special ENEMY) must be marked with a t; if it is not, look higher 
up the table until you find one. If there isn't an enemy marked with a t higher on the table, re-roll for another enemy. 
All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 8 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 8th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed you destroy the entity and the mission is completed successfully and you 
receive the [S] reward.

Whilst performing a top secret mission a special agent has gone missing and needs rescuing. The corporation
has marked the recovery of the agent as a high priority and has assigned the mission as urgent.

DETAILS: Explore until 11 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 11th area has been fully dealt with you en-
counter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission is completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.

In the [SYSTEM] system a large number of gravity mines have accidentally been dropped by a passing ship and the own-
er [NPC] must now foot the bill to have them cleared up before a major incident occurs.
GRAVITY MINES (SM): [NPC] wants you to tractor beam 1d10+10 gravity mines from zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] 
system. Then drop them off at [PORT] the star system's port (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months).
When you generate a zone for the gravity mines, it must not be in a zone with a space port. Once a zone is established 
add the number of gravity mines that need to be tractor beamed from the zone. Then, whenever the captain is in the 
zone, you may perform the TRACKER BEAM test. Each time the test is passed successfully 1d3 gravity mines have been 
caught by the starship's tractor beam. You may perform the test as many time as you like to load up the tractor beam 
with as many gravity mines as the starship is capable of transporting; this is equal to the starship's WS value. When the 
captain has a number of gravity mines in the tracker beam they would like to transport, they must move to the zone 
where the star system's port is located and drop them off. However, each time the SPACE CRUISE test is performed the 
ship is using up extra power at the rate of -1 PL per gravity mine it is transporting. For instance: a ship that passes or fails 
a SPACE CRUISE test that is moving with 4 gravity mines in its tractor beam will use up -5 PL in total; that is -1 PL for the 
standard power consumption to move and -4 PL for each of the gravity mines it is transporting. 
TRACKER BEAM - Test: Int -20, +/- CM, +/- DT [S: -1 AP, -1 PL, tractor 1d3 gravity mines] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL, perform 
Detonation Check] (Pilots).
Once the ship is in the zone with the space port it automatically drops off the gravity mines (no need to dock) and you can 
then deduct the number you have dropped off from the remaining total that needs to be tractor beamed out of the zone. 
When all gravity mines have been dropped off at the port the mission is a completed and the captain receives the reward.
Detonation Check: If the test is failed you must perform a detonation test; call out a number between 1 and 100 and 
then roll 1d100. If you roll the number you called out, one of the gravity mines has detonated and everything for miles 
around is sucked towards it. The captain's starship and the remaining mines are pulled in at a breathtaking speed and 
impact upon one another, causing the remaining mines to detonate. The captain's starship is destroyed and hundreds 
of objects are pulled in towards the gravitation field that has now formed in this part of space. For the captain, the mis-
sion and the game is now over, see the Game Over event. Only by spending a life point can the captain save themselves 
from this catastrophic event and ignore the failed detonation check.

Lost Crew

Arena:
You can feel the excitement in the air. One of the arenas is being 
opened later today and tickets are half price. The buzz is every-
where and it would be a shame to miss out. The arena is usually 
a great deal of fun and has a lot going on. Acts vary from star 
system to star system; however, they all follow a general trend 
with performances of opera, modern music, comedy, dance, acro-
batics, mime, magic etc.
The base cost of a ticket is 100c you must then augment the cost 
by the current star system's reward adjustment x10. 
Example: Jacob is at a space station in a poor star system. The 
system's reward adjustment is -2 $. He multiples -2 x 10 for a total 
of -20. He buys the ticket for 80c (100-20=80).
When the ticket has been bought and you have deducted the cal-
culated number of credits from the log sheet shade 4 Action Pips 
(AP) on the action tracker, and then roll 1d6 on the list below to 
see how the arena visit went.
1.	
The captain is robbed, see the Robbed event.
2.	
The captain is attacked, see the Hostile event.
3.	
The captain meets someone, see the Romance event.
4.	
The captain is enticed to some gambling at the arena's bar, 
see the Gambling event.
5.	
The captain overhears a rumour, see the Rumour event.
6.	
The captain's spirits are lifted (+1 Karma).
Arrengale:
The Arrengale are a race of free roaming galactic space pirates. 
They have no home world, no government, or political structure. 
They fly through space along ancient migration routes they have 
used for centuries; living off space as they go, and stealing what-
ever they need to survive. Their ships are impressively large, and 
fitted with high tech weaponry and advanced defence systems. 
You check the scanner again and again and then sigh nervously. This 
is not going to end well. An Arrengale vessel has just dropped out 
of warp and is arming its weapons. Then, a voice calls out over the 
comms, "Surrender your vessel." The voice is calm and has a strong 
Arrengaley accent. "Lower you shields and prepare to be boarded. If 
you resist we will destroy you." The ship is ten times the size of the 
largest ship you have ever seen and you count twenty forward phaser 
cannons and ten particle beams. You have no choice but to surrender.
Roll 1d100 and deduct the current star system's threat level. If 
the result is 10, or less the Arrengale pirates take the captain's 
starship and sell the captain into slavery, see the Sold Into Slav-
ery event. If the result is 11 or more continue reading.
The Arrengale pirates strip the captain's ship back to its bare bones, 
and then lets them on their way. Remove all modifications, cargo, 
passengers, and crew from the captain's starship. All passengers 
and crew are sold into slavery. The number of crew and passen-
gers you remove are added to the Compensation section on the 
log sheet as compensation must be paid for them.
If the captain has no modifications, cargo, passengers, or crew 
onboard at the start of this event, the Arrengale take the cap-
tain's starship from them and sell the captain into slavery, see 
the Sold Into Slavery event.
Attacked:
The moment you set off for the starship, you hear a noise from 
behind. You turn to see a figure. They are full of anger and are 
looking for trouble. They prepare their weapons and attack.
See the Hostile event. If you manage to kill the hostile it's kill re-
ward is: [K: A/K/W].
Avalanche:
The weather outside is frightful and is blowing a gale. You careful-
ly plot a safe route back to the ship. It takes you alongside some 
high ground, and then all of a sudden the snow gives way into an 
avalanche and you slide and are engulfed. 
Test AVALANCHE below. If you pass the test successfully the cap-
tain has dug out of the snow and reached the shuttle that will 
take them to the starship. If the test fails you must test again and 
continue to perform the test until it is either passed successfully, 
or you have failed the test 4 times. On the 4th failed test, the 
captain has managed to find their way to the shuttle which will 
fly them to the starship.
AVALANCHE – Test: Str -20 [S: -1 AP, -1d3 HP, reached shuttle] 
[F: -1 AP, -1d3 HP] (Strong)
Beneficiary:
You are so saddened at the loss of life. You remember the good 
times you spent together and wish the years could have been 
longer. The caring and love you shared towards one another had 
grown over the years, but nonetheless you were surprised to find 
out you had been a beneficiary in their will. 
Roll 1d10 on the chart below to find out what the departed cap-
tain has left the new captain in their will. If you're instructed to 
roll for a random item, roll on the departed captain's log sheet. 
All items the departed captain leaves to the new captain are re-
moved from the departed captain's log sheet and added to the 
new captain's log sheet.
1d10 Bequeathed
The captain inherits a worthless item, but with a high sen-
timental value. You may add "Worthless item with senti-
mental value" to the log sheet (if you desire).
The captain inherits a random "Small Equipment Pack" 
item. Roll 1d10 until an item in the Small Equipment Pack 
is scored. If there are no items in the Small Equipment 
Pack see result 1 (above).
The captain inherits a random "Large Equipment Pack" 
item. Roll 1d10 until an item in the Large Equipment Pack 
is scored. If there are no items in the Large Equipment 
Pack see result 2 (above).
The captain inherits a random "Utility Belt" item. Roll 
1d6 until an item in the Utility Belt is scored. If there are 
no items in the Utility Belt see result 3 (above).

1d10 Bequeathed
The captain inherits a random "Armour" slot item. Roll 
1d6 until an item in an Armour slot is scored. If there are 
no items in any of the Armour slots see result 4 (above).
The captain inherits a random "Weapon" slot item. Roll 
1d6. On a result of 1-3 the "Weapon slot item is left; on a 
result of 4-6 the Weapon slot item is right. If there are no 
items in either of the Weapon slots see result 5 (above).
The captain inherits all of the credits in the "Credits" box. 
If this is less than 500c, see also result 6 (above).
The captain inherits a random "Cybercon™ implant". 
Roll 1d10 until a Cybercon™ implant in the Cybercon™ 
unit is scored. The implant can either be installed, or 
added to the Small Equipment Pack with a base value 
of 800c. If there are no implants in the Cybercon™ Unit 
see result 7 (above).
The captain inherits the departed captain's Starship, 
cargo and any modifications it has installed. Any crew 
onboard can be dismissed or kept on. As the new cap-
tain is currently at a space dock, crew that are dismissed 
do not need to be jettisoned into space in an escape 
pod and so incur no expense. Any compensation costs 
the ship had, no longer need to be paid, but any costs 
for escape pod do. This payment is made if the ship is 
sold, or kept (see below).
As your captain has two starships, one must be sold be-
fore leaving the space port; and you must initiate a Ship-
yard activity to sell one of the starships. If you're using 
the Changing Economy rules don't forget perform the 
necessary price checks etc. 
The captain inherits everything, see results beginning 
from 9 to 1 (i.e. begin from result 9, then 8, then 7 etc.).
Bio Farm:
On the way to the ship you scan the area and pick up a large quan-
tity of organic material a few miles away from your current loca-
tion. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and fly over to 
investigate and find the area was once a small farm growing and 
handling organic produce but only a few months ago went out 
of business. The site is completely empty apart from a number of 
crates of food that is going to spoil in the next few months. 
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking 
what’s already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to de-
termine how many units of food you may add to the ship's car-
go hold (space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANS-
FER CARGO test below as many times as you like to transfer as 
much, or as little of the cargo you like to the captain's ship.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Bio Waste Dump:
On the way to the ship you scan the area and pick up a large quantity 
of bio waste a few miles away from your current location. Back at the 
ship you take one of the shuttles and fly over to investigate and find 
the area was once a small refinery handling waste products, but only 
a few months ago went out of business. The site is completely empty 
apart from a number of sealed barrels of refined bio waste. 
As there are no personnel around to buy the refined bio waste 
from, you can just take what's already been prepared for ex-
port. Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of bio waste 
you may add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, 
you may perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below as many 
times as you like to transfer as much, or as little of the cargo 
you like to the captain's ship.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Blessed:
You hear a commotion and head over to see what's going on. A 
small biped alien is standing on a crate and is talking to a crowd 
of onlookers. They look in a trance and you stand for a moment to 
listen to what is being said. You hear the words, they are in a lan-
guage you understand, yet the words are jumbled together and 
make no sense. You shrug and walk away. A short while later in a 
quieter part of the space port something lucky occurs.
-1 AP. Roll on table L - Lucky Events.
Borrowed:
You are very surprised that the relative showed up, but are very 
disappointed by what they have to say.
If the captain is not currently at a space port add a trigger arrow 
g to the current star date and make the following date entry: 
"[DATE] At the start of the next port phase you begin, a relative 
who borrowed money arrives, see the Borrowed event." Then 
continue with the game.
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
Providing the captain is at a space port continue reading.
Around a month ago the captain loaned a relative some cred-
its. Today the captain meets the relative and is disappointed 
when the relative asks to borrow another 1d3x100 credits. 
They promise they will pay back all the credits they owe in 
another months time.
If the captain declines to loan them the credits, or has insuffi-
cient funds, the relative finds a way to rob them; see the Robbed 
event. If the captain loans the credits shade the star date 1 
month and 1d6 days in the future. Then make the following date 
entry: "[DATE] A relative who borrowed money arrives, see the 
Borrowed event.

Brawl
You raise your fists and face your opponent. The pair of you stand 
sizing each other up and then it begins!
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
The captain has been drawn into a fight and must perform a se-
ries of tests until either the captain, or their opponent is knocked 
out. During the tests you will be generating a KO number. The KO 
number begins at 5 and if it reaches 0 the opponent has been 
knocked out; however, if the KO result reaches 10 the captain 
has been knocked out. There are 3 types of tests the captain may 
choose; however, the same test may not be performed in succes-
sion. If the fight isn’t going the captain's way, they may consid-
er drawing a weapon and attacking; if they do, gain +1 Law, and 
see the Hostile event; then, if they manage to kill their opponent 
they may choose to steal some items, see the Stealing event.
PUNCH – Test: Str [S:-1 KO] [F:+1 KO] (Strong)
DODGE – Test: Dex [S:-1 KO] [F:+1 KO] (Agility)
TACTICS – Test: Int [S:-1 KO] [F:+1 KO] (Aware)
When a side has been knocked out the brawl is over. If the cap-
tain's opponent was knocked out, the captain suffers -1d3 HP 
from the fight and may now take some of their opponent’s pos-
sessions, see the Stealing event. 
If the captain was knocked out, they suffer -1d6 HP and may 
have some of their items stolen whilst they are unconscious. 
Roll 1d100 and apply the current Star System's Threat Level to 
check, then: If the Brawl event was caused by an event relating 
to a theft, the captain will be robbed on a result of 70 or less, 
otherwise they will be robbed on a result of 40 or less. If the 
captain is robbed, see the Robbed event.
Bugs
On the way to the starship you're attacked by a large swarm of 
insects. They are around a foot in size and have wings that crackle 
with energy as they flap up and down franticly. They are flying 
everywhere and appear interested in your Cybercon™ unit, and 
anything you're carrying with a power cell. Suddenly they lash out 
with bites and stings. You begin thrashing and fighting your way 
towards the safety of the shuttle which will take you to the ship.
Test SWARM below. If you pass the test successfully the captain 
has reached the shuttle that will take them to the starship. If the 
test fails you must test again and continue to perform the test 
until it is either passed successfully, or you have failed the test 
4 times. On the 4th failed test, the captain has managed to find 
their way to the shuttle that will fly them to the starship.
Each time the captain fails the SWARM test, they could have been 
infected and gain an Infection point. At the end of the Bugs event, 
if the captain has any Infection points, see the Parasite event and 
make a PARASITE test; however, when making the PARASITE test 
add the number of Infection Points you have accrued during this 
event to the d100 roll (i.e. if you have 10 Infection points. You 
would roll 1d100+10 when performing the PARASITE test).
SWARM – Test: Dex -15 [S: -1d3 HP, +1 Acid, shuttle reached] [F: 
-1 AP, -1d3 HP, +1 Acid, +5 Infection Points] (Dodge)
Canteen
Just before heading back to the ship, you take a moment to relax 
in one of the canteens and then something happens.
-1d3+1 AP. Roll 1d10 below to find out what happens.
1.	
BRAWL: The captain is bumped and their drink is knocked 
out of their hand. It's obvious this was no accident and the 
captain is drawn into a bar fight. See the Brawl event.
2.	
WRONG IDENTITY: The captain's every move is being 
watched. When the captain leaves the canteen they are con-
fronted. See the Identity event.
3.	
FREE DRINK: A stranger buys the captain a drink and they 
spend a few hours talking. When they leave, the captain spots 
the stranger is hiding a mutation. See the Mutant event. 
4.	
THEFT: The captain is bumped into at the bar. Perform the 
THEFT test below. If the test is successful, the captain must 
decide how to deal with the thief; either by attacking them 
(+1 Law, see the Hostile event), fighting them (see the 
Brawl event), reporting them (see the Report event), or do 
nothing. If the test fails, the captain loses ½ their current 
credits (rounding up) and are only aware of the theft once 
the thief has long gone. 
THEFT - Test: Int -1d100 [S: Hostile event, +1 Law/ Brawl 
event/ Report event/ Do nothing] [F: Deduct ½ the number 
of credits rounding up] (Aware, Lucky)
5.	
GAMBLING: The captain is invited to play some games, see 
the Gamble event.
6.	
STOLEN STARSHIPS: The captain is approached and asked if 
they would like to buy a starship, see the Starship event. 
7.	
FRIEND: The captain gets talking with another customer and 
instantly hits it off. After a few hours the captain offers them 
free transport onboard their starship to get them closer to 
home; see the Stranger event.
8.	
STEALING: The captain spots a group leaving, but one of 
them has left some belongings behind. The captain may, 
if they wish try and take them without the rest of the can-
teen's customers noticing, see the Stealing event.
9.	
CHEAP AS CHIPS: The captain is approached by a work-
er over at the Uranographer quarter who has a data chip 
going cheap. He will also install it free of charge. Roll 1d3 
below to find out which chip he has for sale and follow the 
instruction if the captain decides to buy it.
1.	
Star System Data Chip (Cost: 2000c): Roll 1d100 and 
look up the result on the current hex sheet. If the 
space already has a star system, roll again until an 
empty space is found. When an empty space is found, 
generate a star system there, see Adding Star Systems.
2.

Capture
You feel a hand on your shoulder and turn to see a group has 
gathered. They knock you to the ground and begin to fasten your 
hands and legs together with restraining cables.
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
The captain must struggle to break free by making a number of 
STRUGGLE, WRIGGLE, and TRICK tests. During the tests you will be 
generating a Break Free (BF) number. The BF number begins at 5, 
and if it reaches 0 the captain has managed to break free; however, 
if the BF result reaches 10 the captain is captured and restrained. 
There are 3 types of tests the captain may choose from; however, 
the same test may not be performed in succession.

Confront
You make yourself known and confront the thieves. They aren't 
impressed and look like they are expecting the trouble. You make 
the accusation loud enough for everyone in the vicinity to hear 
that they stole your starship and wait for their reaction.
Roll 1d6 to see how they react to the captain's accusation.
1.	
With Extreme Violence: All but one of the thieves turn and 
run off into the space port. The one that remains draws their 
weapon and attacks; see the Hostile event. The captain will 
get back the stolen starship only if they defeat the attacker. 
If the captain escapes the combat; see the On The Look Out 
event and choose another option to deal with the thieves. 
2.	
With Mild Violence: All but one of the thieves turn and run 
off into the space port. The one that remains raises their 
fists and begin swinging; see the Brawl event. The captain 
will get back the stolen starship only if they manage to score 
a knockout, or kill the thief. If the captain is knocked out; see 
the On The Look Out event and choose another option to 
deal with the thieves.
3.	
Deny The Theft: The thieves deny their involvement in the 
theft and claim they bought the starship from a trader at a 
space port in another star system. The captain shows the 
footage of them stealing the starship and the thieves run off 
and escape; see the On The Look Out event and choose an-
other option to deal with the thieves.
4.	
Demand Proof: The thieves demand some kind of proof, and 
so the captain shows them the starship's documentation and 
the footage recorded on a hand scanner of them stealing the 
starship. One grabs the hand scanner, whilst the other grabs the 
documentation; both then charge off into the port, whilst the 
other produces a forged document proving they have owned 
the starship for a number of years. They inform the captain they 
will take the matter to the port authorities and claim it's the 
captain who is the thief (gain +1 Law). See the On The Look Out 
event and choose another option to deal with the thieves.

ship's activation codes before fleeing. The captain gets back 
the stolen starship.

the starship's activation codes before fleeing. The captain gets 
back the stolen starship and finds 1d6x1000c onboard.

Cyborg Attack
The history of the Cyborgs: The Biological Eradication Agency (BEA) was destroyed over a millennium ago. Its goal was to research and 
build prototype androids that could detect and eliminate micro-organisms causing sickness and disease throughout the galaxy. In a des-
perate attempt to save the company from financial ruin the BEA replaced factory workers with droids at a number of its facilities. A decade 
later and profits were up; the directors seized the opportunity to make more money and replaced their engineers and scientists with cyborg 
research units. These research bots were programmed to program and develop new eliminator bots. Soon the Assassinator model, the 
Enforcer model, and the Destroyer model were flooding the market and the directors were swimming in credits. The units were advertised 
to not only eliminate micro threats but could also be used to run security details, enforce crowd control, police star ports and even used as 
cyber soldiers during a war. Then, due to the cyber wars in the last millennium, it all went wrong for the BEA. Millions and millions of cyborg 
soldiers were being built every month so rival corporations and governments could go to war without suffering any loss of biological life. 
However the research bots and droids at the factories didn’t see it this way; to them millions of their own kind were being slaughtered so 
the “Bios” (the name given to the biological beings) could live without consequence. They rose up and eliminated the directors, and began 
a strategy to gain domination over all biological life forms across the galaxy. They now build themselves and have become a recognised 
race by the Galactic Defence League (GDL). They are a scourge to all biological life forms, whom they seek to destroy and will kill on sight. 
As well as a huge army of cyborg soldiers, they have built thousands of starships to move troops around the galaxy. They will attack any 
starship they come across, whenever their scanners show it has biological life onboard.
A very large starship appears on the long range proximity scanner warning you of an intercept. It has no life signs onboard and no 
authorised security signatures. It has no business to approach your starship. You program a few evasive manoeuvre into the navigation 
computer, but the ship compensates to maintain an intercept. As the ship comes in to view your heart sinks, it is a cyborb vessel. You feel 
sick to the stomach and expect the worst. Desperately you try to engage the jump drive, but the cyborg vessel is using a disruptor and 
the signal is scrambling your controls. You stare out at the ship trying to think of something to do, and then several lights flash across 
the open space from the cyborg ship to yours. You're too late, they are onboard!
The cyborg have boarded the captain's starship and are now in 
the process of eliminating any crew, and passenger onboard; 
as well as the captain. Roll 2d10 on the Cyborg Chart (on the 
right) to determine the cyborg the captain is confronted with 
and begin combat. The cyborg attacking the captain will never 
try to escape combat and all results it makes on the reaction 
table that would result in it escaping are ignored.
Each Security crew member onboard will fight alongside the 
captain. Therefore, each group of 5 Security crew members (or 
part of) gives the captain +10 to their attack characteristic (ei-
ther Str, Dex, or Int) and +2 damage bonus.
Example: If there are 1-5 Security crew onboard, the captain 
gains +10 to their attack characteristic and +2 Dmg. If there are 
6-10 Security crew onboard, the captain gains +20 to their at-

Mutant
Centuries ago in a distant galaxy, a biowarfare laboratory created 
a disease to infect and mutate DNA. The disease was so highly 
contagious it spread across space like a wildfire. In an effort to 
get it under control, a Kill Mutants On Sight (KMOS) policy was 
introduced. Now two thousand years on and it is extremely rare to 
discover a mutant, but every so often sightings are reported and 
when they are special forces are activated to hunt them down and 
exterminate them. 
There isn’t a known cure for those infected with the disease, but a 
few optimistic mutants speculate that somewhere in the laboratory 
where the disease was developed, is the bio-coding needed to pro-
duce a cure. However, the biowarfare laboratory has never been 
discovered and its whereabouts is now lost in time.
If the captain already has the Mutant disease, you need do nothing 
further and can continue with the game, otherwise please read on.
Unfortunately, the captain has been in contact with a mutant and 
now fears they have the disease. Roll 1d100-30, if the result is 
equal to or less than the captain's primary HP they have man-
aged to avoid the disease and you may continue with the game; 
otherwise, the captain has contracted the Mutant disease and 
must shade the star date 1d10+20 days in the future. Then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and 
something does not feel right. See the Mutated event."

The captain will modify their appearance and adjust equip-
ment in order to try and hide their mutations; this occurs 
automatically and you do not need to keep track, but you 
do need to determine if the captain will be discovered whist 
performing port activities. 
The general public may spot the mutation and alert the 
authorities, or the port may have Mutant Hunters on the 
look out for potential targets. Mutant Hunters will kill on 
sight and ask questions later. Therefore, at the start of any 
port phase after the docking phase has been completed 
you must perform one of the DISCOVERY test below. Which 
one is determined by the type of port the captain is dock 
at. The test is modified by the captain's current Discovery 
Value (DV), and so the more mutations the captain has, the 
harder it will be for them to remain undiscovered.
Also, if the port is marked with "(MPOI)" after its name on 
the Star Systems & Zones sheet, you must add +10 to the 
d100 roll when you make the test. This is because the cap-
tain has previously been identified at the port for being a 
mutant and the port authorities are on the look out for an-
yone matching their description. 
If the test is passed successfully you may continue the port 
phase as normal; otherwise, the captain has at some time 
during the port phase been identified as a mutant, see the 
Discovered event.
DISCOVERY 
 – Test: Int -DV [S: Continue with the port 
phase as normal] [F: Captain is identified as a mutant, see 
Discovered event] (Aware)
DISCOVERY 
 – Test: Int -10, -DV [S: Continue with the 
port phase as normal] [F: Captain is identified as a mutant, 
see Discovered event] (Aware)

Narcotics Stash
The long range scanners alert you to a strange magnetic iron pattern 
around a small asteroid field. You change course to investigate and 
when you reach the asteroid field you find it is in fact a cluster of 
crates floating in space. The magnetic iron pattern is caused by a high 
tech plasma net that is holding the crates in a group and preventing 
them from floating away. You scan a crate and manage to bypass the 
interference caused by the net and find that it is filled with narcotics.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of narcotics you 
may add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you 
may perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the 
cargo to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as 
little of the cargo you like that is available. If you take any of the 
narcotics gain +1 Law.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
New Habit
After the away mission you feel alive, full of energy, and hyped up. 
You can't help wondering if the space dust you took has somehow 
chemically imbalanced your body and mind. After a while the ef-
fects wear off and you feel a little out of it and vulnerable.
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event and 
delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer applies. 
If the captain already has a value recorded in the Habit section 
on the log sheet, this event comes to an end; otherwise read on.
Add 9 to the Habit section on the log sheet. The captain now has 
a craving to use more space dust. Each time the captain begin an 
away mission you must roll 1d100. If the result is equal to or less 
than the captain's current habit value, the captain must immedi-
ately use a space dust item on the log sheet. If the captain does 
not have any space dust items on the log sheet they suffer -10 Str, 
-10 Dex, and -10 Int for the entire Away Mission. A reminder of 
this is also shown on the log sheet in the Habit section.
Now that the captain has a mild habit forming. They may feel 
the need to visit a space dust seller from time to time. There-
fore during a port phase, if the captain's habit value is 1 or more 
they may seek out a space dust seller, and you refer to the Deal-
er Of Space Dust event. A reminder of this is also shown on the 
log sheet in the Habit section.
If at anytime the captain's habit value is ever reduced to 0 they 
no longer have a habit and no longer need to check if they need 
to have any space dust before an away mission.
Nomads
On the way back to the starship you spot a group of figures moving 
towards you in the distance. Your scanner doesn’t pick up any weap-
on signatures and so you're fairly certain they are unarmed. When 
you're closer, they are friendly and ask you to join them at their 
camp a few miles away. Luckily it's in the direction you're heading 
towards your starship. They're nomads and appear to be from a 
low tech civilization. You pull a cloak over yourself to hide as much 
of your equipment as you can. At the camp you're ushered through 
a powered doorway into a stone complex, much like a fortification. 
The place is a city rather than a mere camp with hundreds of peo-
ple going about their business. Your translator must have struggled 
to interpret their word for city and came up with camp, unless of 
course the nomads lied. You begin to feel quite nervous and start to 
worry, if this has been a huge mistake!
-1d3 AP. Roll 1d6 to see what happens at the nomad city.
1.	
The captain is taken a prison camp within the city and is 
judged for a crime they neither understand or committed; 
see the Sold Into Slavery event.
2.	
The captain is robbed and then thrown out of the city, see 
the Robbed event.
3.	
The captain is treated suspiciously by the other nomads 
and is attacked by a mob and beaten (-1d10 HP). If the cap-
tain survives the beating, they are thrown out of the city 
and left for dead. The captain makes it back to the ship.
4.	
The nomads want to share food and water and some stories. 
The captain gains 1d3 rations and picks up a rumour; see the 
Rumour event.
5.	
The nomads want to sell the captain 1d6 goods they have 
acquired. For each good they have for sale, choose one of 
the following tables: Table A, K, N, TA, or W. Then roll on the 
chosen table to see what is being offered for sale. The cap-
tain is free to buy any or none of the items that are offered.
6.	
The nomads are healers and want to heal the captain's 
wounds; restore all lost HP. If the captain didn't have any 
wounds to heal (i.e. HP is at maximum), they instead offer 
the captain the following item which you may add to the 
log sheet: (XL) MED PACK: Use to replenish up to 10 lost HP. 
The Med Pack is worth 200c.
Not Paid
You have failed to repay a loan and the organisation you bor-
rowed the credits from has alerted the authorities. They are not 
happy and demand justice.
Remove all shaded days and trigger 
arrows g that relate to the unpaid 
loan and place a line through all of its 
date entries. The matter is now in the 
hands of the authorities. Next, gain 4 
Law, and then if the captain is docked 
at a port see the Law event, other-
wise see the Tracked Down event."

Old Age
You wake after passing out and find yourself in a white room, in a 
bed, and with the man you saw on your communications screen. 
He is looking down at you.
"It didn't go well I'm afraid. We tried to buy you some time; but it's 
old age catching up with you I am afraid. Nothing can be done" 
You thank the doctor for trying and are relieved to find out that 
the surgery was funded by a research program he is involved with, 
so no charge. You spend some days in recovery and are transport-
ed back to your ship. 
Mark off 1d3+6 days on the Star Date Chart. 
On The Look Out
You reduce speed and listen out for the docking anchors to latch 
onto the ship. You hear the clanking sound and count four. With 
the ship safely docked you head for the airlock and step out onto 
the platform. As you pass other vessels, you keep an eye out for 
your old ship. It was stolen a short while ago and you hope one 
day to see it again. 
To determine if you find your stolen ship follow the instructions 
below.
Note: If the captain's starship is returned to the captain, it has 
been stripped of all modifications and there is no cargo on-
board. For reference: the captain's old starship's model type 
can be found in the date entry which triggered this event. 
1.	
Count the number of days that have elapsed since the theft. 
This will be from the date marked with the trigger arrow g 
that triggered this event. If the result is 99, or less go to 
step 2. If the result is 100 or higher, your ship is long gone 
and will never be seen again; well by you at least. Place a 
line through the date entry that triggered this event and 
delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no longer 
applies; then, end this event and continue with the game.
2.	
Roll the 1d100; if the result is equal to, or more than the 
number of days that have expired, the captain spots their 
old starship, go to step 3; however, if the result is lower the 
ship is nowhere to be seen and this event comes to an end.
3.	
Place a line through the date entry that triggered this event 
and delete its trigger arrow g from the star date; it no 
longer applies. Next choose 1 of the 4 options below.
a.	
Do nothing and let the theft go unanswered.
b.	 Contact the port's authorities with the details of the 
theft of the starship. See the Report event. If the crim-
inal is punished the starship is returned to the captain.
c.	
Confront the thieves. Shade 1d10 Action Pips (AP). 
This is the time it takes for the thieves to return to the 
stolen starship. Then see the Confront event.
d.	 Steal back the starship. See the Stealing A Starship 
event. If the event is successful the captain steals back 
their ship.
Outpost
You can see on the scanners that there is a small outpost just a short 
distance away. You zone in on the directions and change course.
-1d3+1 AP. If the captain has just finished an away mission the 
outpost shows up on their scanner when on the way back to the 
starship. Roll 1d10 below to find out what happens in the Outpost.
1.	
BRAWL: The captain is bumped at a bar and their drink is 
spilt. It's obvious this was no accident and the captain is 
drawn into a bar fight. See the Brawl event.
2.	
WRONG IDENTITY: The captain's every move is being 
watched. When they are about to leave they are confronted. 
See the Identity event.
3.	
FREE DRINK: A stranger buys the captain a drink at a bar and 
spends a few hours talking. When they leave, the captain 
spots they are hiding a mutation. See the Mutant event. 
4.	
THEFT: The captain is bumped into at a bar. Perform the THEFT 
test below. If the test is successful, the captain must decide 
how to deal with the thief; either by attacking them (+1 Law, 
see the Hostile event), fighting them (see the Brawl event), re-
porting them (see the Report event), or do nothing. If the test 
fails, the captain loses ½ their current credits (rounding up) 
and are only aware of the theft once the thief has long gone. 
THEFT - Test: Int -1d100 [S: Hostile event, +1 Law/ Brawl 
event/ Report event/ Do nothing] [F: Deduct ½ the number 
of credits rounding up] (Aware, Lucky)
5.	
GAMBLING: The captain is invited to play some games, see 
the Gamble event.
6.	
STOLEN STARSHIPS: The captain is approached and asked if 
they would like to buy a starship, see the Starship event. 
7.	
FRIEND: The captain gets talking with another visitor to the 
outpost and instantly hits it off. After a few hours the cap-
tain offers them free transport onboard their starship to get 
them closer to home; see the Stranger event.
8.	
STEALING: The captain spots some belongings that are unsu-
pervised. They have probably been left behind by accident. 
The captain may if they wish try to take them without any-
one at the outpost noticing, see the Stealing event.
9.	
CHEAP AS CHIPS: The captain is approached by a work-
er over at the Uranographer quarter who has a data chip 
going cheap. He will also install it free of charge. Roll 1d3 
below to find out which chip he has for sale and follow the 
instruction if the captain decides to buy it.
1.	
Star System Data Chip (Cost: 2000c): Roll 1d100 and 
look up the result on the current hex sheet. If the 
space already has a star system, roll again until an 
empty space is found. When an empty space is found, 
generate a star system there, see Adding Star Systems.
2.	
Hyper Jump Data Chip (Cost: 1000c): Choose any Star 
System on the hex sheet and perform step 5. Jump Lanes 
and Step 6: Light Years of the Adding Star Systems rules.
3.	
Deep Space Hyper Jump Data Chip (Cost: 2500c): See 
Moving Between Sectors, Linking Sectors.
10.	 MISSION: An advertisement console inside a bar is inter-
rupted with news of a request for help. See Generating Op-
erations and generate an operation.

Overwhelmed
The moment you have docked you set off for the port's authorities 
and report the location of the starship you found floating in space. 
-1d3 AP. The owner is informed and overwhelmed by the cap-
tain's honesty. They immediately transfer some credits as a re-
ward. Gain 6000c and then place a line through the date entry 
that triggered this event and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies.
Parasite
You have been infected with a parasite and now feel very ill. You 
spend some time resting as your body fights off the effects.
Mark off 1d6 days on the Star Date Chart. Then test PARASITE be-
low. If the test is successful, after many days of rest the captain's 
immune system has managed to fight the parasite and kill it, but 
it has left them weakened -1d3 HP. If you fail the test the parasite 
has affected the captain more seriously, roll 1d6 for the type of par-
asite on the list below and look up how it has affected the captain.
PARASITE – Test: Str [S: -1d3 HP] [F: Roll for Parasite] (Strong)
Parasite: Roll 1d6 to determine the type of parasite:
1.	
Zika: A mild form of Dnegue (-1d6 HP).
2.	
Chikungunya: Fever, headache, muscle/joint pains, swelling, 
rash (-1d10 HP).
3.	
Jungle Worm: Shade the star date 6 months +1d10 days in 
the future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A 
while ago the captain was infected with a parasite and now 
feels very ill, see Jungle Worm event."
4.	
Dengue: High fever, headache, vomiting, muscle/joint pains, 
skin rash (-1d6+6 HP).
5.	
Typhoid: High fever, headache, muscle/joint pains, cough, 
constipation, sickness (-1d10+6 HP). Make the RECOVERY 
test below. If the test fails, only a life point can turn the re-
sult into a success.
RECOVERY – Test: Str -10 [S: -10 Primary STR] [F: Death, see 
the Game Over event] (Strong)
6.	
Malaria: Shade the star date 4d10 days in the future. Then 
make the following date entry: "[DATE] A short while ago the 
captain was infected with a parasite and now feels very ill, 
see Malaria event."
Pawnbrokers
You check out some of the quieter parts of the space port and no-
tice a pawnbrokers. You peer in and see some great items for sale. 
-1 AP. Roll 1d100 +30 on table TA, then roll 1d100 +20 on table 
TB, and then roll 1d100 +10 on table TC. The 3 results you gen-
erate are items for sale at the Pawnbrokers. The captain may 
buy any of the items generated for the price shown by the ta-
bles. Armour is sold undamaged.
Pharmaceutical Plant
On the way to the ship you scan the area and pick up a large quan-
tity of medicine a few miles away from your current location. Back 
at the ship you take one of the shuttles and fly over to investigate 
and find the area was once a pharmaceutical plant that produced 
medicines and health care equipment, but only a few months ago 
went out of business. The site is completely empty apart from 
sealed crates of medicine. 
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking 
what’s already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to deter-
mine how many units of medicine you may add to the ship's car-
go hold (space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANS-
FER CARGO test below as many times as you like to transfer as 
much, or as little of the cargo you like to the captain's ship.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Plagued
On the way back to the ship you stumble and fall, and end up in a 
heap on the ground. A little dazed you stand and begin brushing 
yourself down. You look down to see why you fell, and spot a rot-
ting corpse. You reel in horror, you have walked into an exposed 
graveyard and all around are the corpses of rotting aliens.
Shade 1d6 pips of plague, then make a plague check.
Poisoned
On the way back to the ship you stumble and fall, and end up in a 
heap on the ground. A little dazed you stand and begin brushing 
yourself down. Then it hits you. An intense pain in your leg and you 
peel back your clothing and armour to see a bug-like creature. It has 
wrapped itself around your leg and has two fangs buried deep in your 
flesh. The creature is several inches across and has a powerful grip, 
which is tightening. You swipe at it several times, until reluctantly it 
lets go and drops to the floor. It looks up taunting you with its mouth 
wide open and grinning. Acid drips from its mouth. You raise your 
weapon to finish it off, but it heads off at an alarming pace. 
Shade 1d6 pips of acid, then make an acid check.
Quarantine
All across the port you can hear warning sirens. You stop a mo-
ment to read an advertisement screen, which shows "QUARAN-
TINE IN PROGRESS". A group of armed guards are gathering peo-
ple up and taking them to stand in a long line. They are queuing 
to be tested for a disease that has broken out, and it's not long 
before you're placed in a line too. You wait hours before being 
tested, and  luckily you aren’t infected. Everyone who is cleared of 
disease must leave the port immediately.
Shade 1d6+4 Action Pips (AP) on the action track. Next add 
"Quarantine" to the port's zone. Add a trigger arrow g to the 
current star date and then make the following date entry: "[DATE] 
When the captain enters a zone marked "Quarantine" roll 1d10, 
on a roll of 1 or 10 remove "Quarantine" from the zone. Until 
"Quarantine"is removed from a zone, its port may not be used."

Report
You're the victim of a crime and have decided the best course of 
action is to report it to the star system's authorities and let them 
handle the details.
Roll 1d100 and apply the current star system's threat level mod-
ifier. If the result is 50 or less, the star system's criminal justice 
system does not act quickly enough, or do not care enough to 
intervene. However, If the result is 51 or more they act immedi-
ately and manage to find the criminal. The criminal is punished 
according to the law for their crimes; and any items or credits 
that were stolen are returned to the captain.
Furthermore, if the criminal is punished they may seek some 
kind of revenge on the captain for getting them into trouble. 
Roll 1d100 and apply the current star system's threat level mod-
ifier. If the result is 51 or more the criminal takes their punish-
ment without a thought of revenge. However, if the result is 50 
or less, the criminal seeks revenge, shade the star date 2d10+30 
days in the future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] 
A criminal that was punished when the captain report them to 
the authorities seeks revenge. See the Revenge event."
Rescue
In orbit around a large asteroid you can see a small craft. It ap-
pears lopsided and looks stuck in a gravitational pull. Scanning 
for life forms reveals just one. You turn the ship towards the craft 
and plot a course.
-1d3 AP. You may if you like set up a rescue by performing the RES-
CUE test below. You may perform the test until it is passed success-
fully, or you have failed the test 4 times. On the forth failed attempt 
the craft is pulled into the asteroid and is destroyed. 
If you pass the test successfully you manage to transport a life form 
aboard your ship just before the craft is pulled into the asteroid 
and is destroyed, see the Stranger event. 
RESCUE - Test: Int -10 +/- CM [S: -1 PL, see the Stranger event] [F: 
-1d3 PL] (Transports)
Relative
You're stopped by someone you don't recognise and they say 
"Hey! It's me. We're related. Don't you remember me?"
-1 AP. The captain meets up with a distant relative. Roll 1d6 to 
see what happen:
1.	
Loan: The captain and the relative spend some time talking. 
Then the relative asks to borrow some money. They ask for 
1d3x100 credits, and will pay it back in a month. If the cap-
tain declines the loan, or has insufficient funds, the relative 
robs them; see the Robbed event. If the captain loans the 
credits shade the star date 1 month and 1d6 days in the fu-
ture. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A relative 
who borrowed money arrives, see the Borrowed event."
2.	
Theft: The captain and the relative spend some time talking, 
and then part ways. When they’ve gone the captain notices 
some of their credits have gone missing (- 1d100 credits). 
If the captain has less credits than the number stolen, then 
remove all of the credits the captain has from the log sheet.
3.	
Travelling: The captain and the relative spend hours talking 
(-1d3 AP). The relative is on a long trip and is heading in the 
same direction as the captain. The captain gives them pas-
sage on the starship. Shade the star date 1d10+20 days in 
the future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A 
relative onboard is about to disembark. Whilst onboard they 
have also become a dear friend, see the Disembark event."
4.	
Shame or Fame: The relative spends some time talking 
about the family, and tells them of a distant relative the 
captain knew nothing about. The relation in question, for 
a time was widely well-known for their deeds. Generate a 
NPC's name and Occupation by rolling 3 times on table (GB) 
N – Names; then roll 1d3 modified by the NPC's Occupation 
reward value ($) (if it has one). If the result is 1 or less the 
captain deducts -1 Rep. If the result is 2 nothing happens, if 
the result is 3 or more the captain gains +1 Rep.
5.	
Karma: The captain and the relative spend some time talk-
ing, and eventually it is time for them to leave. The meeting 
was enjoyed by all and spirits were lifted (+ 1 Karma).
6.	
The Inheritance: The relative informs the captain they have 
tracked them down because they have inherited some mon-
ey from a distant, but wealthy relation (+1d6x1000 credits).

Revenge
You look across the room and spot a face in the crowd and your heart 
sinks. You know that trouble is heading your way!
If the captain is not currently docked at a space port, ignore this 
event for now; instead, add a trigger arrow g to the current star 
date and then make the following date entry: "[DATE] When the 
captain next docks at a space port roll 1d10, on a roll of 1-6 see 
the Revenge event."
If you have been directed here by a trigger arrow (i.e. you rolled 1-6 
on a d10), place a line through the date entry and delete its trigger 
arrow g from the star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
If the captain is docked at a space port an act of revenge is com-

to see what happens.

acid pips on the acid track and then make an acid check.
2.

plan to hand the captain over to the port authorities with

the star date 1d10+3 days in the future. Then make the fol-
lowing date entry: "[DATE] The captain a short whiles ago

Rifter
Rifters are an ancient order going back six millennia. They use 
mind control and telekinesis to perform all kinds of strange and 
mystical effects. The Rifter Program was created in the last cen-
tury and outlaws the use of Rifter "Wizardly" in all but a few star 
systems. Wherever the program is upheld, the Rifters have moved 
underground and are still practicing their powers.
Every life form in the galaxy is built upon an energy that keeps them 
alive. Those that have unlocked the secrets of this energy and can 
use it for wondrous effects are known as Rifters. The captain has 
been given an insight into the power of the Rifters and must now 
decide if they will embrace the Rifter way of life, or not. If the cap-
tain decides to be a Rifter there is no turning back; and all of the 
following rules will apply for the duration of the captain's life; so 
please read through them carefully before making a decision.
1.	
Shade the Rifter box (found on the front of the new log sheet 
under the tracks section) to activate the Rifter rules. This sig-
nifies the captain is now a Rifter. 
2.	
Shade the box on the Rifter skill (found where the experi-
ence star is usually located). it's now active and can be used. 
There isn’t a skill bonus yet, but one can be gained through 
using its experience track (just like the other skills).
3.	
Rifters are generally frowned upon by law enforcers. They 
have a tendency to speak out against the law and politics 
and are known to interfere in the affairs of governments 
and star systems. Therefore, as a Rifter the captain will al-
ways have a minimum Law value of 1, and a maximum Rep 
value of 9. If necessary make the adjustments to Law and 
Rep to conform to these restraints.
4.	
As a result of manipulating their inner power, most Rifters 
adopt a natural yearning to help out and assist, especially 
those in less fortunate situations. For this reason a Rifter 
captain must always tackle an Instant Mission when one 
is available, and they are not permitted to take the fail op-
tion. In addition, each time the captain docks at a Space 
Station 
, before they take any port activities they must 
spend 1 hour (-1AP) visiting the homeless shelters at the 
port; where they hand out some credits to those in need 
(-100c). If the captain has insufficient credits record them 
as a negative value; however, by the end of the port phase 
the captain must have 0 credits or more, even if it means 
they have to borrow some money (see the Loan event). 
5.	
The moment the captain becomes a Rifter, they have un-
locked the first Rifter Ability. Shade the ① pip on the Rifter 
Abilities track. This means the captain may now use the first 
ability shown on the Rifter Ability Chart found on the oppo-
site page. Until others are shaded, they cannot be used.
6.	
Rifter Abilities can be used at anytime, but only when they're 
applicable. They are marked with (Combat), and (Non-Com-
bat) as a further guide. Those marked (AM) can only used 
whilst on an Away/Instant Mission. Note: Combat abilities 
do not require a combat action to use. When the captain 
uses a Rifter Ability it also cost energy and you must shade a 
number of pips equal to the ability's energy cost on the ener-
gy track, then you perform the RIFTER test below. The ener-
gy cost is shown as ⓪①②③and④. Note: If there isn't 
enough energy pips to shade, the ability cannot be used. If 
the test fails you must test the captain's energy level. 
RIFTER - Test: Int -20 [S: Ability takes effect] [F: Make an 
ENERGY TEST] (Rifter)
ENERGY TEST: Roll 1d10 and if the result is equal to or less 
than the number of pips shaded on the energy track the 
captain's energy levels are compromised (-1d3 HP). 
7.	
If you make a RIFTER test and score a natural roll of 10 or less, 
you may either shade 2 pips on the Rifter skill's experience 
track, shade 1 pip on the Int experience track, or replenish 1d3 
power (i.e. remove shaded pips equal to the number rolled). 
However, if you score a natural 5 or less, you may perform 
one of the above options, or alternatively roll for a new Rifter 
Ability. To roll for a new Rifter Ability, roll 1d10 on the Rifter 
Abilities Chart and if the ability rolled is not already shaded on 
the log sheet you gain that ability and can go ahead and shade 
it. However if you generate an ability the captain already has 
acquired, no new Rifter Ability is gained on this occasion.
8.	
Energy is naturally replenished each time a day is checked off 
on the Star Date Chart at the rate of 1 energy per day. There-
fore, each day the captain spends on an away mission (show-
ing ⊞ on the Star Date Chart) or checks off on the Star Date 
Chart replenishes 1 energy (i.e. 1 shaded pip is removed).

Ripe For The Taking
Your scanners pick up a starship dead in space. It has no life signs 
onboard and is just drifting. You change course and perform some 
further scans and discover the ship was abandoned due to an radi-
oactive particle leak. The decontamination period has long passed 
and the logs show the owner was meant to return to the ship many 
years ago. However, the anchor motors have perished and have al-
lowed the ship to drift. The owner probably has no idea where their 
ship now is. Galactic law requires anyone finding the ship to report 
it to the nearest space port. However, you could just tow the ship to 
the nearest port and get its data banks scrubbed. 
-1d3 AP. Roll 1d100+10 on table S - Starships to find out the ship 
the captain has discovered. If the captain decides to take the ship 
for their own gain +1 Law. Then decide which ship will be towed 
and which will be the captain's main ship (as explained in the main 
D100 Space rulebook on p23). Note: The stolen Starship has no 
passengers, crew, or cargo onboard; and no modifications fitted. 
Alternatively, the captain may report the position of the ship next 
time they are at a space port. If they do add a trigger arrow g 
to the current star date and then make the following date entry: 
"[DATE] When the captain next docks at a space port they inform 
the authorities the whereabouts of an abandoned starship they 
discovered floating in space. See the Overwhelmed event."

ment is a little on the light side. You check your packs and pouches, 
and then your armour and holsters and find some things are miss-
ing. You have been robbed!
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
The captain is the victim of theft and has been robbed. Roll 1d6, 
this is the number of items that have been stolen. Then, roll 
1d10 on the list below for each item that has gone missing and 
follow its instructions.

Decoders: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Decod-
ers track go to 2; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on 
the Decoders track.
2.

ä track go to 3; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on the 
Rations ä track.
3.

Vision track go to 4; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on 
the Night Vision track.
4.	
Oxygen: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Oxygen 
O2 track go to 5; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on the 
Oxygen O2 track.
5.	
Power Cells: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Pow-
er Cells track go to 6; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips

Slavery
The judge reads out your sentence and you're condemned to 
spend the rest of your life in slavery. You was hoping for Incarcer-
ation. However, you know the punishment is far better than facing 
a trial by combat. The security droids holding you, march you to a 
holding cell and from there you're transported to a slave ship. You 
have no idea where they have taken you, but after processing you 
find yourself working in a slave mine. Day after day you're taken 
to a small moon to extract minerals in an underground quarry. 
It's hard work, but at least they keep you well fed. You dream of 
escaping and hope one day your dream will come true!
Add 1d6+6 years to the Star Year box on the Star Date Chart. 
This is the number of years that have passed before an escape 
attempt can be made. For each year you add, you must apply 
the Aging modifier, which could end up triggering the Time Is

gered, or if you already have the following entry on the reverse 
of the time sheet: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and are 
feeling terrible. See the Life Expectancy event."; unfortunately 
the captain has died of old age, see the Game Over event. Any 
trigger arrows g, or other shaded dates remain in place, but do 
not activate them or deal with them.

Law to 6 and deduct -4 Rep; they can now begin trying to es-
cape captivity by performing an ESCAPE SLAVERY test each year.

-10 modifier. When performing the test, none of the captain's

sions or a starship, remove all of the following from the log

ygen O2, Night Vision, Rations, Decoders, Power Cells, all Items

The captain is an escaped slave from the [SYSTEM] system. 
When in zone 1 of the [SYSTEM] system, see the Tracked Down

If the test fails, for the next year the captain is placed in a gang

Note: Each year until the captain has escaped you must apply the

ber rolled. Rolls 1d6 for each item, and looks up the result below.

1.	
Roll on table N - Needed.

Roll on table A - Armour.

Stealing A Starship
You look over the starship and she is a beauty. The airlock is wide 
open and you know a few activation codes that might work. You 
look both ways. No one is watching and there are no sign of any 
security drones. The ship is wide open and just begging to be stolen!
If the captain is attempting to steal back a starship that used to be-
long to them, but was stolen, gain +1 Law. If the captain is stealing 
a starship that has never belonged to them, gain +1d3 Law.
If you know the starship's model look it up on table S - Starships; 
otherwise, roll on table S - Starships. The roll is modified by the 
star system's reward adjustment x10.
Example: Jacob doesn’t know the starship's model and so rolls 
1d100 on table S - Starships. He scores a 78. However, because the 
star system is Destitute with a -4 reward adjustment, Jacob must 
adjust 78 with a -40 modifier (-4 x 10 = -40). He looks up result 38 
(78-40=38) on table S and finds the starship is a Cutter Class IV.
Once the starship's model is known, its time to decide if the cap-
tain will go through the theft or not. If they do, they need to first 
get onboard without being seen and then activate it for take off. 
Perform the GAIN ENTRY test below.
GAIN ENTRY - Test: Dex -10 [S: Onboard] [F: Caught, see the Law 
event] (Agility, Aware)
If the GAIN ENTRY test is successful the captain is now onboard 
and must active the starship for take off. Look up the Salvage val-
ue of the starship; this is the modifier you apply to the ACTI-
VATE STARSHIP test below. If the captain is attempting to steal 
back a starship the Salvage value is halved (rounding down).
ACTIVATE STARSHIP - Test: Int -Salvage [S: Starship is Stolen] [F: 
Caught, see the Law event] (Hacking)
If the captain passes the ACTIVATE STARSHIP test successful-
ly they have manage to steal the starship, take off and leave the 
space port. Outside of the space port's scanner range, the captain 
rendezvous with the their current ship. You may then decide which 
ship will be towed and which will be the captain's main ship (as 
explained in the main D100 Space rulebook on p23). Note: The 
stolen Starship has no passengers, crew, or cargo onboard; and no 
modifications fitted.
Stolen Goods
You feel a hand on your shoulder. The surprise makes you jump 
and you turn to see a face partially hidden in the shadows of a 
hooded cloak, "I have some cargo for sale at a good price. If you're 
interested follow me." The figure turns and walks down an alley-
way. You wait a moment and then decide to follow.
If the captain doesn’t wish to buy any stolen cargo, end this event 
and continue with the game. If the captain does wish to buy 
some stolen cargo, the smuggler is offering three different types 
of cargo at half the normal buy price at the port. Perform the 
following procedure 3 times to generate the cargo on offer and 
the quantity of units available. If the captain buys 1 unit or more 
of the stolen cargo gain +1 Law point for handling stolen goods. 
1.	 Using the numbers at the top of the Economy Sheet roll 
1d100 (re-roll results of 1-20) to generate a type of cargo 
being offered. If you happen to roll the same cargo that has 
previously been offered, ignore that result and roll again.
2.	
Roll 1d10+10 for the number of units of cargo that are avail-
able from the smuggler.
3.	
Find the buy price of the cargo at the port the captain is cur-
rently docked at on the economy sheet. For the purpose of 
this event the cargo's buy price is halved (rounding down).
4.	
The captain may buy as much or as little of the cargo be-
ing offered and may even take a Cargo Docks activity to sell 
some non-stolen goods to make room in the cargo hold.

Stolen Starship
You spot in the distance a large group of thugs hanging around 
your starship. They appear to be breaking open the boarding 
hatch to get onboard. Whilst running to intervene, you grab your 
hand scanner, and zoom in to record them. Unfortunately, you ar-
rive too late and your ship takes off for who knows where? They 
have stolen your starship! 
The captain's starship has been stolen. If the captain is not cur-
rently at a space port, they activate a distress beacon on their 
hand scanner and after a few days a passing ship picks them up 
and takes them to the nearest space port. Shade 1d6 days on 
the star chart and update the captain's current location to the 
zone with a space port.
At the space port the captain notifies the authorities, and pro-
vides them with the footage from their hand scanner. Next, 
they fill out several documents to claim on the ship's insurance 
policy. Follow the instructions below in order to handle the in-
surance claim.
1.	
The captain will receive half of the credit value rounding down 
of the ship and all modifications on the log sheet. Then re-
move the starship and all modifications from the log sheet.
2.	
Using the space port's sell prices where the captain is locat-
ed, total up the value of the cargo onboard at the time of the 
theft. The captain receives half of this total rounding down. 
Then remove all cargo from the cargo hold on the log sheet.
3.	
All crew and passengers that where onboard after the theft 
are jettisoned into space. It's the responsibility of the cap-
tain to pay out compensation. Total up the compensation 
costs (see Compensation/Escape Pod# on page 14) from 
the Passenger Manifest and Crew section on the log sheet, 
and remove the credits. Then remove the crew and passen-
gers from the log sheet.
4.	
Next, add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and 
make the following date entry:"[DATE] Your starship, a 
[MODEL] was stolen and you're now on the look out for 
the thieves. When you dock at a space port see the On the 
Look Out event." Replace the word [MODEL] with the mod-
el of the captain's starship.
5.	
You may now begin the port phase. It would be a good idea 
to buy a new ship. If you lack the funds you may acquire a 
loan, see the Loan event.

A large starship drops out of warp directly beside your ship. It's the

through the communication channel "This is a routine stop and

allow a patrol crew to board your vessel. Non-compliance and we

If the captain does not wish to be boarded, they will have to 
fight the stop and search patrol ship, roll 1d10+90 on table S 
- Starships to see which starship the captain will face and then 
decide if they will attack or not. If they attack, conduct a space 
combat with the stop and search patrol ship.
If the captain does not fight the patrol ship, they have no choice 
but to lower the shields and allow a droid patrol onboard. 
If the there is any Contraband, Narcotics, or Weapons onboard

the test is failed, the illegal cargo is discovered and the stop and 
search patrol beams them and the captain back to their ship for 
an arrest, see ARRESTED below.
SMUGGLE - Test: Int [S: Cargo remains hidden] [F: Cargo is dis-
covered, +1 Law, -1000c, all red goods are removed, see AR-
RESTED below] (Aware, Smuggler)
If the captain passes the SMUGGLE test, or didn't have any con-
traband, Narcotics or Weapons onboard. The captain may be 
identified as a wanted fugitive, see below. 
If the captain's Law value is 0 or less, they are not wanted by the 
authorities and have nothing to fear from the stop and search; 
the event is now over. However, if the captain's Law value is

captain's law value, they have been rumbled and the stop and 
search patrol beams them and the captain back to their ship for 
an arrest, see ARRESTED below.

the following date entry: "[DATE] Each time the captain docks 
at a space port roll 1d6, on a result of 1 or 6 the Transcenden-
tal Alien's prediction were correct, [RESULT]". Roll 1d10 on the 
list below and replace [RESULT] on the date entry with the 
information rolled.

Trial By Combat
The judge reads out the sentence of Trial By Combat. You was hop-
ing to be sold into slavery. However, you know the punishment is 
far better than being place in cryo-prison for all eternity. The secu-
rity droids holding you march you to a holding cell and after a few 
hours you're taken to a large arena. 
Roll 1d10+90 on table E - Enemy from the main D100 Space rule-
book. This is the enemy the captain must now fight. Neither the 
captain or the enemy are permitted to escape combat; each re-
sult the enemy rolls on the Enemy Reaction Table that instructs 
them to escape is ignored and they instead fight as normal. The 
captain has all of the equipment that is on the log sheet at the 
time of sentencing and has been given plenty of time to re-equip 
and adjust as many items as they wish before the fight starts. 
The fight is to the death. If the captain is killed see the Game 
Over event. If the captain kills the enemy, they are released and 
you change the captain's Law value to 0 and deduct -2 Rep.
Unlawful Entry
From across the dock you spot a starship. It's a small vessel; little 
more than a shuttle. The airlock is wide open and you stroll over to 
take a peek inside. No one is around and there are no crew insight. 
You see several items that look interesting and wonder if anyone 
would notice if you went aboard to get a better look.
If the captain decides to break galactic law and enter a starship 
without the owner's/operator's consent, gain +1 Law, then see 
the Stealing event.
Velorian Fever
Velorian Fever is the most dangerous illness in all the galaxy. It is 
commonly contracted from a Velorian when they sneeze or sweat. 
The species is so toxic to all other biological life forms they have 
been banned from all non-velorian star systems, and must trav-
el in complete isolation across the galaxy. Even with these con-
straints Velorian Fever does at times breakout across the galaxy.
Whenever the captain's starship enters a star system marked 
with "VELORIAN FEVER" the star system is currently suffering 
from an outbreak of Velorian Fever; and there is a chance whilst 
in the system the captain may become infected.
When in an infected star system, each time the captain checks 
for an event (i.e. after an away mission, instant mission, space 
mission, or when playing the port phase), you must add 1d3 to 
the current "VF" number (the VF number is located in the in-
fected star system's hex on the hex sheet) and then roll 1d100. 
If you roll equal to, or less than the current VF number you must 
perform the VELORIAN FEVER test below. 
VELORIAN FEVER – Test: Int -20 [S: Not infected] [F: Contracts 
Velorian Fever, see Velorian Fever below] (Aware)
Velorian Fever: If the test fails the captain has contracted the 
Velorian Fever and suffers an illness more severe, but very sim-
ilar to Malaria; shade the star date 4d10 days in the future. 
Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A short while ago 
the captain contracted Velorian Fever, an illness very similar to 
Malaria. Deduct -1d10 primary Str, -1d10 primary Dex, -1d10 
primary Int, and -1d6 primary HP, then see the Malaria event."

Wanted Poster
Whilst walking through a busier part of port, you spot an adver-
tisement screen showing a series of wanted posters. The display 
is shuffling through quite a number of different criminals, but one 
catches your eye. You think you have seen them here in port, but 
want to check to be sure. The wanted poster eventually comes 
around again and now you're positive you have seen them and 
only just a few minutes ago!
Roll 2d10 on the Wanted Chart below to find out the crime the 
criminal is wanted for and whether they are wanted dead or 
alive. Then decide if the captain will attempt to find them. If the 
captain goes after the criminal perform the SEARCH test below. 
The SEARCH test can be made multiple times until the criminal 
is found, or the captain gives up in the attempt. If the criminal 
is found you then decide if the captain will attempt to capture 
or kill the criminal based on if the criminal is wanted dead or 
alive. If the criminal is wanted alive, you perform the ALIVE test 
below, and if the criminal is wanted dead or alive, you may per-
form either the ALIVE test below or attack them to take them 
out. The ALIVE test is modified by the Criminals Strength (CS). If 
the ALIVE test is failed, the criminal has managed to escape the 
captain and can no longer be found. If the captain attacks the 
criminal, take note of the Hostile Chart (HC) modifier and then 
see the Hostile event (use the Hostile Chart modifier in place of 
the star system's threat level when rolling on the Hostile Chart).
If the criminal is captured or killed, the captain gains the reward 
shown, but uses up 1d3 Action Pips (AP) in order to hand over the 
criminal to the authorities and fulfil the necessary paper work. 
SEARCH - Test: Int -20 [S: -1AP, criminal is found] [F: -1d3 AP, 
criminal is not found] (Aware)
ALIVE – Test: Str +/- CS [S: Criminal is captured, -1 Law] [F: -1d6+6 
HP, criminal escapes] (Strong)
