War
Across the port you can hear warning sirens booming out and 
across a loud speaker you hear an announcement "WE ARE AT 
WAR!" You spot a squad of armed guards and a group of security 
droids escorting civilians towards a long line of people. The queue 
leads to the docking bay. You hear them telling everyone that the 
port is being evacuated and the consensus is to leave the star sys-
tem as soon as possible. You join the end of the line immediately.
-1d6+4 AP. Next add "AT WAR" to the star system's hex on the 
hex sheet. Add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and 
then make the following date entry: "[DATE] [SYSTEM] is at war. 
When entering [SYSTEM] roll 1d6, on a roll of 1 or 6 a ship at-
tacks, See the Ship Attacks event." Then, shade the star date 
1d3 months and 1d10 days in the future and make the follow-
ing date entry: "[DATE] A war in [SYSTEM] comes to an end. 
Remove the AT WAR from the star system's hex. Then, find the 
trigger arrow on the Star Date Chart relating to the war and 
place a line through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow 
g from the star date; it no longer applies."
Note: You replaced [SYSTEM] with the name of the star system 
the captain is currently in. 

Waste Dump
The long range scanners alert you to a cluster of objects floating in 
an area of space rarely frequented these days. You change course 
to intercept and when they appear on the main display you find 
you have discovered a waste dump. Often high volumes of waste 
are dumped in quieter regions of space by waste sorting facilities, 
when they're overloaded with work. They'll usually be watched by 
security drones to stop the waste from being stolen, but on this 
occasion there are no drones keeping watch.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of waste you may 
add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you may 
perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the cargo 
to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as little 
of the cargo you like that is available. 
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Water Mine
On the way back to the starship you scan the area. You are on the 
lookout for hostile life forms. Luckily the scanner does not pick up 
any dangers, but it does transmit data of a large cavern locat-
ed under the surface that is harbouring a vast amount of fresh 
drinking water. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and 
fly over to investigate. Built at the base of the cavern is a water 
processing plant that extracts the underground water supply, fil-
ters it and pumps it up to the surface where it's stored in large 
containers ready to be shipped. Unfortunately, a few months ago 
the plant went out of business. The site is completely empty apart 
from sealed containers filled with fresh water.
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking what’s 
already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to determine 
how many units of water you may add to the starship's cargo hold 
(space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANSFER CARGO 
test below as many times as you like to transfer as much, or as little 
of the cargo you like to the captain's ship.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Weapon Factory
On the way to the ship you scan the area and pick up a large 
quantity of weapon signatures a few miles away from your cur-
rent location. Back at the ship you take one of the shuttles and fly 
over to investigate and find the area was once a Weapon Factory 
that produced high-end, military grade weapons, but only a few 
months ago went out of business. The site is completely empty 
apart from sealed crates of weapons. 
There are no personnel around to stop you from just taking 
what’s already been prepared for export. Roll 1d10+10 to deter-
mine how many units of weapons you may add to the ship's cargo 
hold (space permitting). Then, you may perform the TRANSFER 
CARGO test below to transfer the cargo to the captain's starship. 
You may transfer as much, or as little of the cargo you like that is 
available. If you take any of the weapons gain +1 Law.
TRANSFER CARGO - Test Int -10, +/- CM [S: -1d3 AP, -1PL, 1d6 
cargo transferred] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Transports)
Wildfire
All around, in every direction there is fire and it's spreading at 
an alarming rate. Off in the distance you see plumes of black 
smoke billowing up from the ground. You're caught in a large 
wildfire that has spread across the area for miles. You program 
your scanner for a safe route to the starship and set off. 
Test WILDFIRE below. If you pass the test successfully the captain 
has reached the shuttle that will take them to the starship. Each 
time the test fails the captain is trapped by a patch of fire and 
you must test FIRE below. After the FIRE test you must continue 
to perform the WILDFIRE test until it is either passed successfully, 
or you have failed the test 4 times. On the 4th failed test, the 
captain has managed to find their way to the shuttle which will 
fly them to the starship.
WILDFIRE – Test: Dex -10 [S: -1 AP, -1d3 HP, reached shuttle] [F: -1 
AP, -1d3 HP, test FIRE] (Escape)
FIRE – Test: Dex -10 [S: Escape fire patch safely] [F: Burnt by the 
fire, -1d3 HP] (Dodge)
Wormhole
The long range scanners have picked up a strange abnormally: 
Several starships have appeared from out of nowhere and all 
within minutes of one another. You turn the ship around and ac-
tivate a long range visual in their direction and discover the ships 
have been using a wormhole. The wormhole is phasing in and 
out of view whenever a ship emerges or enters. You make a note 
of its position on the ship's star map.
Using the captain's current star system roll 1d10 for a zone that 
does not yet have a POI (keep rolling until an empty zone is 
scored). Add the Wormhole POI to the zone and name it in the 
usual way ( see Adding Star Systems, 7.POIs & 9.Naming POIs). 
Then generate the wormhole (see Wormholes).

D10
Details          During an Instant Mission when you roll on table E apply the captain's current star system's threat modifier.
1 
VERMIN CONTROL [S:1d3 Rewards]
An abandoned base near to your location is overrun with vermin. The situation is causing the locals some issues 
and they have put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a c; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a c higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a c you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 4 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 4th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
BUG CONTROL [S:1d3+1 Rewards]
An abandoned base near to your location is overrun with bugs. The situation is causing the locals some issues 
and they have put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a ; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a  higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a  you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 5 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 5th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
THE CRAZY SCIENTISTS [S:1d3+2 Rewards]
A science laboratory near to your location has suffered an infestation that has caused its personnel to go crazy. The corpo-
ration running the lab has put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a t; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a t higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a t you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 6 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 6th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
THE DROID REVOLT [S:1d3+3 Rewards] O2
An industrial plant that relies solely on android staff near to your location has suffered a major insurgence over working 
conditions. The owner has put together a small reward to pay anyone who can enter the base and remove the problem.
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a s; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. 
If there isn't an enemy marked with a s higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) marked with a s you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 7 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 7th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed the mission has been completed successfully and you receive the [S] reward.
HALLUCINOGENIC CHEMICAL [S:1d3+4 Rewards]
A insubstantial entity has lodged itself into the air vents at an off-world military base. The creature is excreting
a hallucinogenic chemical, and the contaminated air has caused the personnel to go utterly mad. 
SPECIAL ENEMY: Roll for the special ENEMY, it must be marked with a ≡ ; if it is not, look higher up the table until you find one. If 
there isn't an enemy marked with a ≡ higher on the table, re-roll for the special ENEMY. The special ENEMY gains +10 HP.
SPECIAL RULES: All enemies you encounter (except the special ENEMY) must be marked with a t; if it is not, look higher 
up the table until you find one. If there isn't an enemy marked with a t higher on the table, re-roll for another enemy. 
All enemies (including the Special ENEMY) you encounter gain +1 Dmg.
DETAILS: Explore until 8 areas have been added to the map sheet. When the 8th area has been fully dealt with you encoun-
ter the special ENEMY. When it has been killed you destroy the entity and the mission is completed successfully and you 
receive the [S] reward.

(GB) O – Operations
D100
SM = Space Mission, AM = Away Mission, O2 = Triggers Oxygen, NV = Triggers Night Vision
Ç = Enemy is an Elite and gains +10 HP and ignores all escape reaction rolls it makes. 
(E##) = E followed by a number tells you which number you will find the enemy on table E - Enemy. 
When a word is shown in CAPITAL letters and in brackets, such as [PORT], (ZONE #), or [SYSTEM] the game is asking you 
to replace the feature with its name (or zone number) found on the sector's Star Systems And Zones Sheet. 
For Away Missions when rolling on table E - Enemy apply the captain's current star system's threat modifier to the roll.
M$
[NPC] knows the whereabouts of a small asteroid that has some remarkable metal properties. Their contacts would like 
to examine the metal from the asteroid and are willing to pay highly for the privilege.
MINING FOR METAL (SM): [NPC] wants you to mine 1d3 x 10 Metals from zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system and 
sell at [PORT] the star system's port. Expires: [DATE] (1d3+3 months).
If the star system has an asteroid, this is where you must mine and the operation is placed in its zone; otherwise, you 
must generate a random empty zone in the star system and place the operation there. Please note: By adding the oper-
ation to an empty zone in this manner does not add a permanent asteroid to the star system; the asteroid will only be 
functional to perform the mission and will only exist until the mission has expired or has been completed.
1$
A food processing plant has been hit by a power surge and has shut down. It has been inoperable for months and the 
shareholders are getting restless. The plant is now quite a dangerous place, and has become overrun with all kinds of 
creatures, droids, and villainous scum. The owner is looking for someone to head on in and investigate the cause of the 
power overload to see if it is a viable option to send in engineers to make repairs.
POWER OVERLOAD (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Explore until 1d3+6 
yellow areas have been added to the map sheet and have been searched. Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months). When the 
last yellow area has been searched the source of the power surge has been discovered and the owner can get it fixed.
If the star system has an agricultural world, this is the zone where the mission is located. If the system doesn’t have 
an agricultural world then you must generate a random empty zone in the star system and place the operation there. 
Please note: By adding the operation to an empty zone in this manner does not add a permanent agricultural world to 
the star system; the agricultural world will only be functional to perform the mission and will only exist until the mission 
has expired or has been completed.
1$
A water processing plant has been hit by a power surge and has shut down. It has been inoperable for months now and 
the shareholders are getting restless. The plant is now quite a dangerous place, and has become overrun with all kinds 
of creatures, droids, and villainous scum. The owner is looking for someone to head on in and investigate the cause of

POWER OVERLOAD (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Explore until 1d3+6

last green area has been searched the source of the power surge has been discovered and the owner can get it fixed.
If the star system has a water world, this is the zone where the mission is located. If the system doesn’t have a water 
world then you must generate a random empty zone in the star system and place the operation there. Please note: 
By adding the operation to an empty zone in this manner does not add a permanent water world to the star system; 
the water world will only be functional to perform the mission and will only exist until the mission has expired or has 
been completed.
1$
A warehouse was closed due to a chemical leak from a container. It has been inoperable for months now and the 
shareholders are getting restless. The plant is now quite a dangerous place, and has become overrun with all kinds of 
creatures, droids, and villainous scum. The owner is looking for someone to head on in and purge the scourge that has 
taken control of the warehouse.
PURGE THE SCOURGE (AM O2 NV): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to Explore 1d3+6 red 
areas and Kill the enemy there (they ignore all escape reaction results). Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months). When the last 
red area and its enemy has been slain the owner can reopen the facility and the mission is completed.
If the star system you generate for the mission's location has a moon, or a dead planet point of interest, then this is 
the zone where the mission is located. If the system has both a moon and a dead planet, you must generate randomly 
between them where the mission will be located. If the system has neither a moon, or a dead planet then you must 
generate a random empty zone where the mission will be located.

There is a huge problem with vermin under the space dock. The port is desperate for anyone to enter the service tunnels and 
terminate them. When proof of the termination is handed over (the scraps) the port's authorities will hand over payment.

An inventor approached a military grade weapon's facility with a prototype weapon. The weapon was so powerful, if it 
ever got constructed it would be a planet-killer. However, whilst the plans were en route a galactic peace activist posing 
as a security guard stole them and hid them inside a security pass. Their intention was to destroy the plans at a later 
time, away from preying eyes. However, there was a mix up and the security pass with the plans got thrown out and 
taken to a dump site, where it is now lost.
SECURITY BREACH (AM O2): In zone [ZONE #] in the [SYSTEM] system [NPC] wants you to enter a dump site and 
Collect (Hand In) 1 Security Pass with the hidden plans, or 1 Objective Item (see operation for details). Expires: 
[DATE] (1 month).
If the star system you generate for the mission's location has a moon, or a dead planet point of interest, then this is 
the zone where the mission is located. If the system has both a moon and a dead planet, you must generate randomly 
between them where the mission will be located. If the system has neither a moon, or a dead planet then you must 
generate a random empty zone where the mission will be located. 
Whilst on the away mission if the captain gains a security pass, it may be the pass with the hidden plans, and you roll 
1d100 to check; if the result is 30 or less then it's the security pass with the hidden plans and the away mission is com-
pleted. Note: If the captain finds a batch of security passes (i.e. the game instructs +2 Pass, or +3 Pass), you do not check 
each individual pass, but instead make one roll for the entire batch. Alternatively, the first Objective Item the captain 
finds is in fact the security pass with the hidden plans and the mission is completed.

tem. Then drop them off at [PORT] the star system's port (see operation for details). Expires: [DATE] (1d3 months).
When you generate a zone for the escape pod's location, it must not be in a zone with a space port. Once a zone is es-
tablished add the number of escape pods that need to be tractor beamed from the zone. Then, whenever the captain is 
in the zone, you may perform the TRACKER BEAM test. Each time the test is passed successfully 1d3 escape pods have 
been caught by the starship's tractor beam. You may perform the test as many time as you like to load up the tractor 
beam with as many escape pods as the starship is capable of transporting; this is equal to the starship's WS value. When 
the captain has as many escape pods as they wish in the tractor beam, they must then move to the zone where the star 
system's port is located to drop them off. However, each time the SPACE CRUISE test is performed to move, the ship 
uses up extra power at the rate of -1 PL per escape pod it is transporting. For instance: a ship that passes or fails a SPACE 
CRUISE test that is moving with 4 escape pods in its tractor beam will use up -5 PL in total; that is -1 PL for the standard 
power consumption to move and -4 PL for each of the escape pods it is transporting. 
TRACKER BEAM - Test: Int -20, +/- CM, +/- DT [S: -1 AP, -1 PL, tractor 1d3 escape pods] [F: -1d3 AP, -1d3 PL] (Pilots). 
Once the ship is in the zone with the space port it automatically drops off the escape pods and you can then deduct the 
number you have dropped off from the remaining total that needs to be tractor beamed out of the zone. When all pods 
have been dropped off at the port the mission is a completed and the captain receives the reward.

ries of tests until either the captain, or their opponent is knocked 
out. During the tests you will be generating a KO number. The KO 
number begins at 5 and if it reaches 0 the opponent has been 
knocked out; however, if the KO result reaches 10 the captain 
has been knocked out. There are 3 types of tests the captain may 
choose; however, the same test may not be performed in succes-
sion. If the fight isn’t going the captain's way, they may consid-
er drawing a weapon and attacking; if they do, gain +1 Law, and 
see the Hostile event; then, if they manage to kill their opponent 
they may choose to steal some items, see the Stealing event.

Confront
You make yourself known and confront the thieves. They aren't 
impressed and look like they are expecting the trouble. You make 
the accusation loud enough for everyone in the vicinity to hear 
that they stole your starship and wait for their reaction.
Roll 1d6 to see how they react to the captain's accusation.
1.	
With Extreme Violence: All but one of the thieves turn and 
run off into the space port. The one that remains draws their 
weapon and attacks; see the Hostile event. The captain will 
get back the stolen starship only if they defeat the attacker. 
If the captain escapes the combat; see the On The Look Out 
event and choose another option to deal with the thieves. 
2.	
With Mild Violence: All but one of the thieves turn and run 
off into the space port. The one that remains raises their 
fists and begin swinging; see the Brawl event. The captain 
will get back the stolen starship only if they manage to score 
a knockout, or kill the thief. If the captain is knocked out; see 
the On The Look Out event and choose another option to 
deal with the thieves.
3.	
Deny The Theft: The thieves deny their involvement in the 
theft and claim they bought the starship from a trader at a 
space port in another star system. The captain shows the 
footage of them stealing the starship and the thieves run off 
and escape; see the On The Look Out event and choose an-
other option to deal with the thieves.
4.	
Demand Proof: The thieves demand some kind of proof, and 
so the captain shows them the starship's documentation and 
the footage recorded on a hand scanner of them stealing the 
starship. One grabs the hand scanner, whilst the other grabs the 
documentation; both then charge off into the port, whilst the 
other produces a forged document proving they have owned 
the starship for a number of years. They inform the captain they 
will take the matter to the port authorities and claim it's the 
captain who is the thief (gain +1 Law). See the On The Look Out 
event and choose another option to deal with the thieves.
5.	
Own Up: The thieves admit the theft and hand over the star-
ship's activation codes before fleeing. The captain gets back 
the stolen starship.
6.	
Own Up and Booty: The thieves admit the theft and hand over 
the starship's activation codes before fleeing. The captain gets 
back the stolen starship and finds 1d6x1000c onboard.

The judge reads out your sentence and you're condemned to spend 
the rest of your life frozen, in a Cryo-Prison. You was hoping for

to being put to death. The security droids march you to a holding 
cell and from there you're transported to a Cryo-Prison. After a 
few days they process the freezing by placing you in a coffin-like 
container made of metal. You lay down inside and a droid lowers 
a lid to seal you in. In the lid is a small window, which you peer out

better view and see the droid bending over to press a button. You 
hear a click, but nothing happens and so it thumps it several times 
and in a tinny voice says "The cryo-chamber has a malfunction. 
The freeze pumps are stuck." It kicks the side and there is a whir-
ring noise. Then an intense pain hits your feet and rapidly spreads 
upwards into your legs, then to your waist, body and head. You 
scream out in pain and as you pass out you hear the droid say

ing off the freeze pumps. Every so often when the chamber de-
activates it gives the captain a chance of escape.

Cyborg Attack
The history of the Cyborgs: The Biological Eradication Agency (BEA) was destroyed over a millennium ago. Its goal was to research and 
build prototype androids that could detect and eliminate micro-organisms causing sickness and disease throughout the galaxy. In a des-
perate attempt to save the company from financial ruin the BEA replaced factory workers with droids at a number of its facilities. A decade 
later and profits were up; the directors seized the opportunity to make more money and replaced their engineers and scientists with cyborg 
research units. These research bots were programmed to program and develop new eliminator bots. Soon the Assassinator model, the 
Enforcer model, and the Destroyer model were flooding the market and the directors were swimming in credits. The units were advertised 
to not only eliminate micro threats but could also be used to run security details, enforce crowd control, police star ports and even used as 
cyber soldiers during a war. Then, due to the cyber wars in the last millennium, it all went wrong for the BEA. Millions and millions of cyborg 
soldiers were being built every month so rival corporations and governments could go to war without suffering any loss of biological life. 
However the research bots and droids at the factories didn’t see it this way; to them millions of their own kind were being slaughtered so 
the “Bios” (the name given to the biological beings) could live without consequence. They rose up and eliminated the directors, and began 
a strategy to gain domination over all biological life forms across the galaxy. They now build themselves and have become a recognised 
race by the Galactic Defence League (GDL). They are a scourge to all biological life forms, whom they seek to destroy and will kill on sight. 
As well as a huge army of cyborg soldiers, they have built thousands of starships to move troops around the galaxy. They will attack any 
starship they come across, whenever their scanners show it has biological life onboard.
A very large starship appears on the long range proximity scanner warning you of an intercept. It has no life signs onboard and no 
authorised security signatures. It has no business to approach your starship. You program a few evasive manoeuvre into the navigation 
computer, but the ship compensates to maintain an intercept. As the ship comes in to view your heart sinks, it is a cyborb vessel. You feel 
sick to the stomach and expect the worst. Desperately you try to engage the jump drive, but the cyborg vessel is using a disruptor and 
the signal is scrambling your controls. You stare out at the ship trying to think of something to do, and then several lights flash across 
the open space from the cyborg ship to yours. You're too late, they are onboard!
The cyborg have boarded the captain's starship and are now in 
the process of eliminating any crew, and passenger onboard; 
as well as the captain. Roll 2d10 on the Cyborg Chart (on the 
right) to determine the cyborg the captain is confronted with 
and begin combat. The cyborg attacking the captain will never 
try to escape combat and all results it makes on the reaction 
table that would result in it escaping are ignored.
Each Security crew member onboard will fight alongside the 
captain. Therefore, each group of 5 Security crew members (or 
part of) gives the captain +10 to their attack characteristic (ei-
ther Str, Dex, or Int) and +2 damage bonus.
Example: If there are 1-5 Security crew onboard, the captain 
gains +10 to their attack characteristic and +2 Dmg. If there are 
6-10 Security crew onboard, the captain gains +20 to their at-
tack characteristic and +4 Dmg.
During the combat with the captain other cyborgs all around 
the ship are killing the crew and passengers. At the start of each 
combat round roll 1d3. This is the number of crew or passengers 
that have been killed by the cyborg. Choose which passengers, or 
crew members are killed from the log sheet and remove them. 
Don't forget to add the number that are killed to the compensa-
tion box. If you cannot remove a passenger or a crew member 
from the log sheet, because none remain, each crew member 
or passenger that you cannot remove is instead converted into a 
+10 AV, and a +1 Dmg modifier that is applied to the cyborg the 
captain is fighting for the forthcoming combat round.
Example: Jacob rolls a 3 for the cyborg's attack on the passengers 
and crew, but only has 1 passenger remaining and no crew. He 
removed the last passenger from the log sheet and the cyborg 
gains +20 AV and +2 Dmg modifier during the next combat round. 
When the combat with the captain is over, so is the cyborg at-
tack on the ship and you can continue with the game.

Hostile Terrain
You emerge from the complex and the environment is in cha-
os. Cycles of engulfing heat are preventing contact with the 
shuttle and the readings on your scanner are performing a loop 
the loop. After an hour, a wind erupts and you're forced to take 
shelter. The wind has brought a more intense heat along with it. 
You're hot and dusty and there is no sign of the day ending and 
the night beginning. After another couple of hours the heat has 
risen again and you're running low on water. You're concerned if 
you do not get back to the shuttle soon you will dehydrate. 
(-1d3+2 AP) You must now perform the HOSTILE TERRAIN test 
below a number of times until the captain reaches the shuttle 
craft that will take them back to the starship. Each time the HOS-
TILE TERRAIN test is performed you will be generating a Progress 
Value (PV). Continue to make the HOSTILE TERRAIN test until you 
have a PV of 6 or more; this will result in the captain reaching the 
shuttle and being transported back to the starship. 
HOSTILE TERRAIN – Test: STR -10 [S: +2 PV, -1d3 HP, -1 AP] [F: +1 
PV, -1d3 HP, -2 AP] (Aware)
Hunted
You charge off looking for a good place to hide. Your pursuers are 
relentless in the chase and you feel you will soon be caught. Af-
ter what seems like hours (-1d6 Action Pips (AP)) you manage to 
shake them and manage to get aboard your starship.
Add a trigger arrow g to the current star date and make the 
following date entry:"[DATE] The captain is being hunted by the 
authorities. At the start of a port phase at [PORT] in the [SYS-
TEM] system, see the Law event." 
Note: When you're recording the date entry replace [PORT] with the 
port's name and the [SYSTEM] with the name of the star system.

ensues it's obviously a case of mistaken identity.

through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.

low to find the captain’s mistaken identity.

Incarceration
The judge reads out your sentence and you are to be incarcerated. 
You was hoping for community service. However, the punishment is 
far better than being sold into slavery. The security droids holding 
you march you to a holding cell and after a few hours you're process 
and transported to a maximum security prison.
The amount of jail time the captain serves depends on their 
current Law value. Look up the captain's Law value below and 
follow its instructions; however, for each year you add, you 
must apply the Aging modifier which could end up triggering 
the Time Is Almost Up event. Note: If it does, or if you already 
have the following entry on the reverse of the time sheet: 
"[DATE] You wake in the morning and are feeling terrible. See 
the Life Expectancy event."; unfortunately the captain has died 
of old age, see the Game Over event. Any trigger arrows g, or 
other shaded dates remain in place, but do not activate them 
or deal with them. If the captain survives the term of imprison-
ment change Law to 0 and continue with the game; you will in 
this case need to resolve any trigger arrows g, or shaded dates 
that apply immediately.
Law is 4: Add 1d3+2 years to the Star Year box and -1 Rep.
Law is 5: Add 1d3+4 years to the Star Year box and -2 Rep
Law is 6: Add 1d3+6 years to the Star Year box and -3 Rep

Jungle Worm
You begin to feel very ill. Your limbs stiffen and sores appear all 
over your body. You have a high fever, headaches, and a sore 
throat, and are fatigued and forced to take bed rest. 
After a week the sores have evolved into large blisters that itch 
and burn. As the days pass the itching lessens, but the burning 
heightens. Now you're in agony. You are dizzy, and vomiting con-
stantly. Then, one by one the sores erupt, and a stinking green pus 
shoots outwards in all directions; from the craters left behind a 
small larvae crawls out.
Mark off 1d6+7 days on the star chart, and the captain suffers 
-1d3 primary HP.

Log Entry
After leaving the mission site, before you can initiate a transport 
back to the ship, you have to follow the standard procedure of 
scanning the area for hostile life forms. You set your scanner to 
proximity and it shows an anomaly directly in front of you. The 
anomaly is fragments of a log entry that is being played over and 
over on repeat. The holographic picture is very faint and until you 
scanned you hadn't even spotted it was there. It shows a captain 
talking, but there is no audio. 
If you wish, you may perform the HACK SCANNER test below 
to recalculate your scanner to a different frequency to find the 
audio. If you do and the test is a success you hear the captain 
explaining details of a mission, see Generating Operations. If 
you fail the test, a power surge causes the scanner to malfunc-
tions, and you decide to give up.
HACK SCANNER – Test: Dex -20 [S: You hear the captain, see 
Generating Operations] [F: Scanner malfunctions] (Hacking)
Long Range Communication
The long range sensors has just picked up a communication be-
tween two starships. They should be transmitting on a secure 
channel, but for some reason your ship's audio transmitter is able 
to pick up every word. There is a little interference which is muf-
fling their voices, but you could steer the ship towards the two 
ships and tweak some settings to help improve the audio. 
If you wish, you may perform the MANOEUVRE test below to 
try and covertly reposition the starship to find out what they 
are talking about. If you do and the test is a success you have 
learnt details of a mission, see Generating Operations. If you fail 
the test, the ships become aware of your eavesdropping and 
switch to a more secure channel.
MANOEUVRE - Test: Int -20 +/- CM, +/- DT [S: You hear 
everything] [F: They notice and switch to secure channel] (Pilot)

Message Sent
A few moments later after sending the message a man in his thir-
ties pops up on your communication screen. He is starting to go 
grey and speaks with a strange accent. Cybercon™ wires are pro-
truding from his head.
"Hello, I am Dr Gurcar Neapman, I have been expecting you; I have 
read through your medical records. Very interesting case indeed. 
I would like you to shuttle over so we can help you." You leave im-
mediately and when you arrive you spot some worker droids, but 
no life forms. You stand for a while and one approaches. It is a ser-
vice droid. You notice a blaster hole through one of its wheels. The 
damage is causing the droid to spin left, whilst the other wheels 
are straining to keep it moving forwards. 
"Good DAY to YOUUuuhiss. I wiLL Be youRrrhiss healTH aSSistan-
thiss TOoodDay. PleeAASSE FolloWwhiss MeeeE." The droids 
speech is way off and in need of a good calibration. Its volume is 
up and down and some words trails off into a static hiss. You fol-
low the droid down a long windowless corridor to a small white 
room. At the centre is a white metal bed with a flat white pillow. 
A retractable light is flickering on and off above the bed. Around 
the room are several low level cupboards with metal worktops 
laid out with various medical equipment; mostly scanners, me-
chanical forceps, and laser knives, but there are a few primitive 
surgeon tools and plenty of metal dishes and suction hoses. Near 
the door is a trolley loaded with 2 waist high canisters. Digital 
regulators are fixed to the top. On the bed is a data pad with 
a questionnaire which the droid instructs you to fill out. It's a 
typical consent form for surgery. When you’ve finished, the droid 
takes the pad and turns awkwardly on its damaged wheel and 
makes for the door.
"PleeAASSE laAayhiis onhiss thEe BEDddhiss Annd YoUUUur sur-
geon wiLL Be with YOUUuuhiss shortlyeehiss." The droid stops at 
the canisters and presses a button; you hear a faint beep and then 
it continues through the door. Something does not seem quite 
right and you have a bad feeling. When you walk to the door it 
shuts. There is no switch, or button on the inside. You hear another 
beep and one of the canisters jolts, then gas escapes from its regu-
lator. A moment later, the other canister jolts too and gas escapes. 
They mix in the air and a blue fog fills the room. Holding your 
breath, you keep as low as possible looking for a way to escape. 
You reach the bed and trip, and land on the floor. You're struggling 
to hold your breath but the fall causes you to take in a breath and 
immediately you pass out.

Mutant
Centuries ago in a distant galaxy, a biowarfare laboratory created 
a disease to infect and mutate DNA. The disease was so highly 
contagious it spread across space like a wildfire. In an effort to 
get it under control, a Kill Mutants On Sight (KMOS) policy was 
introduced. Now two thousand years on and it is extremely rare to 
discover a mutant, but every so often sightings are reported and 
when they are special forces are activated to hunt them down and 
exterminate them. 
There isn’t a known cure for those infected with the disease, but a 
few optimistic mutants speculate that somewhere in the laboratory 
where the disease was developed, is the bio-coding needed to pro-
duce a cure. However, the biowarfare laboratory has never been 
discovered and its whereabouts is now lost in time.
If the captain already has the Mutant disease, you need do nothing 
further and can continue with the game, otherwise please read on.
Unfortunately, the captain has been in contact with a mutant and 
now fears they have the disease. Roll 1d100-30, if the result is 
equal to or less than the captain's primary HP they have man-
aged to avoid the disease and you may continue with the game; 
otherwise, the captain has contracted the Mutant disease and 
must shade the star date 1d10+20 days in the future. Then make 
the following date entry: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and 
something does not feel right. See the Mutated event." 

Mutated
This morning when you awoke you felt strange and it suddenly be-
came apparent; the mutant you encountered a few weeks ago has 
infected you with the mutant disease and a mutation has surfaced.
The captain is now a mutant, there is no known cure. Near the 
top of the new style log sheet is a Mutant box. Shade the box to 
signify the captain is now a mutant 
The captain will need to be very careful or run the risk of being 
discovered as a mutant. The penalty is immediate death. Next 
to the Mutant box is a DV box where you will record the cap-
tain's Discovery Value, the higher this value the more chance 
there is the captain will be discovered. On the reverse of the log 
sheet is a section called "Mutations", this is where you record 
the mutations and any special rules they have; there is space for 
four mutations (the maximum). The following rules now apply 
for the mutated captain. 
When you're first directed to this event complete step 1 and gen-
erate the captain's first mutation.
1.	
Mutations: Each time the captain is instructed to gain a 
mutation follow the instructions below:
1.	
Roll 1d00 on the Mutation Chart (see below) and add 
the mutation to the Mutations section on the reverse 
of the log sheet. Note: A mutation will only manifest 
itself once, if you generate a mutation the captain al-
ready has, ignore the result and roll again for another. 
2.	
Add 5 to the captain's Discovery Value (DV).
3.	
If the captain now has four mutations ignore this step, 
otherwise shade the star date 1d10+90 days in the fu-
ture, and make the following date entry: "[DATE] You 
awake in the morning and something does not feel 
right. See the Mutated event and generate another 
mutation (step 1)." 
2.	
The Cure: Whenever the captain begins an away mission, 
there is a chance that somewhere on the mission the captain 
may come across the bio-coding needed to produce a cure. 
The chances are extremely low; however, before the mission 
roll 1d100; on a result of 100 it's possible the captain may find 
the bio-coding in the form of an Objective Item. The first ob-
jective item you add to the log sheet whilst on the mission is 
the bio-coding. Next, the captain must find a batch of chemi-
cals to be loaded into a special bio-chamber. This is where the 
captain will lay and be injected with the chemicals. Therefore, 
the second Objective Item added to the log sheet is the batch 
of chemicals. When the two Objective Items (The bio-coding 
and the batch of chemicals) have been added to the log sheet, 
the captain must then find the bio-chamber. Each green area 
you add to the map sheet from this point on, roll 1d6. On a 
result of a 1 or a 6 do not roll for its geographic feature, in-
stead it contains the bio-chamber. Remove the two objective 
items from the log sheet and then remove all mutations from 
the log sheet and the shading from the mutant box. The cap-
tain is no longer a Mutant and has been cured. Note: When a 
mutation is removed, if it made an adjustment to a primary 
characteristic (i.e. BIG HEAD, TRIPLE JOINTED, BIG ARMS etc.) 
the adjustment must be reversed. 
3.	
Port Phase: The following rules apply when the captain is at 
a Space Station 
 or a Military Dock 
 :
The captain will modify their appearance and adjust equip-
ment in order to try and hide their mutations; this occurs 
automatically and you do not need to keep track, but you 
do need to determine if the captain will be discovered whist 
performing port activities. 
The general public may spot the mutation and alert the 
authorities, or the port may have Mutant Hunters on the 
look out for potential targets. Mutant Hunters will kill on 
sight and ask questions later. Therefore, at the start of any 
port phase after the docking phase has been completed 
you must perform one of the DISCOVERY test below. Which 
one is determined by the type of port the captain is dock 
at. The test is modified by the captain's current Discovery 
Value (DV), and so the more mutations the captain has, the 
harder it will be for them to remain undiscovered.
Also, if the port is marked with "(MPOI)" after its name on 
the Star Systems & Zones sheet, you must add +10 to the 
d100 roll when you make the test. This is because the cap-
tain has previously been identified at the port for being a 
mutant and the port authorities are on the look out for an-
yone matching their description. 
If the test is passed successfully you may continue the port 
phase as normal; otherwise, the captain has at some time 
during the port phase been identified as a mutant, see the 
Discovered event.

phase as normal] [F: Captain is identified as a mutant, see 
Discovered event] (Aware)

Report
You're the victim of a crime and have decided the best course of 
action is to report it to the star system's authorities and let them 
handle the details.
Roll 1d100 and apply the current star system's threat level mod-
ifier. If the result is 50 or less, the star system's criminal justice 
system does not act quickly enough, or do not care enough to 
intervene. However, If the result is 51 or more they act immedi-
ately and manage to find the criminal. The criminal is punished 
according to the law for their crimes; and any items or credits 
that were stolen are returned to the captain.
Furthermore, if the criminal is punished they may seek some 
kind of revenge on the captain for getting them into trouble. 
Roll 1d100 and apply the current star system's threat level mod-
ifier. If the result is 51 or more the criminal takes their punish-
ment without a thought of revenge. However, if the result is 50 
or less, the criminal seeks revenge, shade the star date 2d10+30 
days in the future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] 
A criminal that was punished when the captain report them to 
the authorities seeks revenge. See the Revenge event."
Rescue
In orbit around a large asteroid you can see a small craft. It ap-
pears lopsided and looks stuck in a gravitational pull. Scanning 
for life forms reveals just one. You turn the ship towards the craft 
and plot a course.
-1d3 AP. You may if you like set up a rescue by performing the RES-
CUE test below. You may perform the test until it is passed success-
fully, or you have failed the test 4 times. On the forth failed attempt 
the craft is pulled into the asteroid and is destroyed. 
If you pass the test successfully you manage to transport a life form 
aboard your ship just before the craft is pulled into the asteroid 
and is destroyed, see the Stranger event. 
RESCUE - Test: Int -10 +/- CM [S: -1 PL, see the Stranger event] [F: 
-1d3 PL] (Transports)
Relative
You're stopped by someone you don't recognise and they say 
"Hey! It's me. We're related. Don't you remember me?"
-1 AP. The captain meets up with a distant relative. Roll 1d6 to 
see what happen:
1.	
Loan: The captain and the relative spend some time talking. 
Then the relative asks to borrow some money. They ask for 
1d3x100 credits, and will pay it back in a month. If the cap-
tain declines the loan, or has insufficient funds, the relative 
robs them; see the Robbed event. If the captain loans the 
credits shade the star date 1 month and 1d6 days in the fu-
ture. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A relative 
who borrowed money arrives, see the Borrowed event."
2.	
Theft: The captain and the relative spend some time talking, 
and then part ways. When they’ve gone the captain notices 
some of their credits have gone missing (- 1d100 credits). 
If the captain has less credits than the number stolen, then 
remove all of the credits the captain has from the log sheet.
3.	
Travelling: The captain and the relative spend hours talking 
(-1d3 AP). The relative is on a long trip and is heading in the 
same direction as the captain. The captain gives them pas-
sage on the starship. Shade the star date 1d10+20 days in 
the future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] A 
relative onboard is about to disembark. Whilst onboard they 
have also become a dear friend, see the Disembark event."
4.	
Shame or Fame: The relative spends some time talking 
about the family, and tells them of a distant relative the 
captain knew nothing about. The relation in question, for 
a time was widely well-known for their deeds. Generate a 
NPC's name and Occupation by rolling 3 times on table (GB) 
N – Names; then roll 1d3 modified by the NPC's Occupation 
reward value ($) (if it has one). If the result is 1 or less the 
captain deducts -1 Rep. If the result is 2 nothing happens, if 
the result is 3 or more the captain gains +1 Rep.
5.	
Karma: The captain and the relative spend some time talk-
ing, and eventually it is time for them to leave. The meeting 
was enjoyed by all and spirits were lifted (+ 1 Karma).
6.	
The Inheritance: The relative informs the captain they have 
tracked them down because they have inherited some mon-
ey from a distant, but wealthy relation (+1d6x1000 credits).

Revenge
You look across the room and spot a face in the crowd and your heart 
sinks. You know that trouble is heading your way!
If the captain is not currently docked at a space port, ignore this 
event for now; instead, add a trigger arrow g to the current star 
date and then make the following date entry: "[DATE] When the 
captain next docks at a space port roll 1d10, on a roll of 1-6 see 
the Revenge event."
If you have been directed here by a trigger arrow (i.e. you rolled 1-6 
on a d10), place a line through the date entry and delete its trigger 
arrow g from the star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
If the captain is docked at a space port an act of revenge is com-
mitted against the captain for something that occurred in the 
captain's past. Roll 1d6 and look up the result on the list below 
to see what happens.
1.	
Acid: The captain is exposed to a toxic chemical. Shade 1d3 
acid pips on the acid track and then make an acid check.
2.	
Capture: An attempt to capture the captain is made. They 
plan to hand the captain over to the port authorities with 
allegations of false crimes; see the Capture event.
3.	
Infection: They infect the captain with an parasite; shade 
the star date 1d10+3 days in the future. Then make the fol-
lowing date entry: "[DATE] The captain a short whiles ago 
was infected with a parasite; see the Parasite event." 
4.	
Theft: They steal from the captain; see the Robbed event.
5.	
Fight: They have brought a friend to start a fight with the 
captain; see the Brawl event.
6.	
Attack: They have brought a friend to attack the captain; 
see the Hostile event.
Rifter
Rifters are an ancient order going back six millennia. They use 
mind control and telekinesis to perform all kinds of strange and 
mystical effects. The Rifter Program was created in the last cen-
tury and outlaws the use of Rifter "Wizardly" in all but a few star 
systems. Wherever the program is upheld, the Rifters have moved 
underground and are still practicing their powers.
Every life form in the galaxy is built upon an energy that keeps them 
alive. Those that have unlocked the secrets of this energy and can 
use it for wondrous effects are known as Rifters. The captain has 
been given an insight into the power of the Rifters and must now 
decide if they will embrace the Rifter way of life, or not. If the cap-
tain decides to be a Rifter there is no turning back; and all of the 
following rules will apply for the duration of the captain's life; so 
please read through them carefully before making a decision.
1.	
Shade the Rifter box (found on the front of the new log sheet 
under the tracks section) to activate the Rifter rules. This sig-
nifies the captain is now a Rifter. 
2.	
Shade the box on the Rifter skill (found where the experi-
ence star is usually located). it's now active and can be used. 
There isn’t a skill bonus yet, but one can be gained through 
using its experience track (just like the other skills).
3.	
Rifters are generally frowned upon by law enforcers. They 
have a tendency to speak out against the law and politics 
and are known to interfere in the affairs of governments 
and star systems. Therefore, as a Rifter the captain will al-
ways have a minimum Law value of 1, and a maximum Rep 
value of 9. If necessary make the adjustments to Law and 
Rep to conform to these restraints.
4.	
As a result of manipulating their inner power, most Rifters 
adopt a natural yearning to help out and assist, especially 
those in less fortunate situations. For this reason a Rifter 
captain must always tackle an Instant Mission when one 
is available, and they are not permitted to take the fail op-
tion. In addition, each time the captain docks at a Space 
Station 
, before they take any port activities they must 
spend 1 hour (-1AP) visiting the homeless shelters at the 
port; where they hand out some credits to those in need 
(-100c). If the captain has insufficient credits record them 
as a negative value; however, by the end of the port phase 
the captain must have 0 credits or more, even if it means 
they have to borrow some money (see the Loan event). 
5.	
The moment the captain becomes a Rifter, they have un-
locked the first Rifter Ability. Shade the ① pip on the Rifter 
Abilities track. This means the captain may now use the first 
ability shown on the Rifter Ability Chart found on the oppo-
site page. Until others are shaded, they cannot be used.
6.	
Rifter Abilities can be used at anytime, but only when they're 
applicable. They are marked with (Combat), and (Non-Com-
bat) as a further guide. Those marked (AM) can only used 
whilst on an Away/Instant Mission. Note: Combat abilities 
do not require a combat action to use. When the captain 
uses a Rifter Ability it also cost energy and you must shade a 
number of pips equal to the ability's energy cost on the ener-
gy track, then you perform the RIFTER test below. The ener-
gy cost is shown as ⓪①②③and④. Note: If there isn't 
enough energy pips to shade, the ability cannot be used. If 
the test fails you must test the captain's energy level. 
RIFTER - Test: Int -20 [S: Ability takes effect] [F: Make an 
ENERGY TEST] (Rifter)
ENERGY TEST: Roll 1d10 and if the result is equal to or less 
than the number of pips shaded on the energy track the 
captain's energy levels are compromised (-1d3 HP). 
7.	
If you make a RIFTER test and score a natural roll of 10 or less, 
you may either shade 2 pips on the Rifter skill's experience 
track, shade 1 pip on the Int experience track, or replenish 1d3 
power (i.e. remove shaded pips equal to the number rolled). 
However, if you score a natural 5 or less, you may perform 
one of the above options, or alternatively roll for a new Rifter 
Ability. To roll for a new Rifter Ability, roll 1d10 on the Rifter 
Abilities Chart and if the ability rolled is not already shaded on 
the log sheet you gain that ability and can go ahead and shade 
it. However if you generate an ability the captain already has 
acquired, no new Rifter Ability is gained on this occasion.
8.	
Energy is naturally replenished each time a day is checked off 
on the Star Date Chart at the rate of 1 energy per day. There-
fore, each day the captain spends on an away mission (show-
ing ⊞ on the Star Date Chart) or checks off on the Star Date 
Chart replenishes 1 energy (i.e. 1 shaded pip is removed).

Ripe For The Taking
Your scanners pick up a starship dead in space. It has no life signs 
onboard and is just drifting. You change course and perform some 
further scans and discover the ship was abandoned due to an radi-
oactive particle leak. The decontamination period has long passed 
and the logs show the owner was meant to return to the ship many 
years ago. However, the anchor motors have perished and have al-
lowed the ship to drift. The owner probably has no idea where their 
ship now is. Galactic law requires anyone finding the ship to report 
it to the nearest space port. However, you could just tow the ship to 
the nearest port and get its data banks scrubbed. 
-1d3 AP. Roll 1d100+10 on table S - Starships to find out the ship 
the captain has discovered. If the captain decides to take the ship 
for their own gain +1 Law. Then decide which ship will be towed 
and which will be the captain's main ship (as explained in the main 
D100 Space rulebook on p23). Note: The stolen Starship has no 
passengers, crew, or cargo onboard; and no modifications fitted. 
Alternatively, the captain may report the position of the ship next 
time they are at a space port. If they do add a trigger arrow g 
to the current star date and then make the following date entry: 
"[DATE] When the captain next docks at a space port they inform 
the authorities the whereabouts of an abandoned starship they 
discovered floating in space. See the Overwhelmed event."
Robbed
You suddenly pause as something does not feel right. Your equip-
ment is a little on the light side. You check your packs and pouches, 
and then your armour and holsters and find some things are miss-
ing. You have been robbed!
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
The captain is the victim of theft and has been robbed. Roll 1d6, 
this is the number of items that have been stolen. Then, roll 
1d10 on the list below for each item that has gone missing and 
follow its instructions. 
1.	
Decoders: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Decod-
ers track go to 2; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on 
the Decoders track.
2.	
Rations: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Rations 
ä track go to 3; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on the 
Rations ä track.
3.	
Night Vision: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Night 
Vision track go to 4; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on 
the Night Vision track.
4.	
Oxygen: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Oxygen 
O2 track go to 5; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips on the 
Oxygen O2 track.
5.	
Power Cells: If the captain has no shaded pips on the Pow-
er Cells track go to 6; otherwise, remove 1d3 shaded pips 
on the Power Cells track.
6.	
Utility Belt: If the captain's Utility Belt is empty go to 7; 
otherwise, roll 1d6 until an item stored in the Utility Belt is 
scored and remove that item from the log sheet.
7.	
Small Pack: If the captain's Small Equipment Pack is emp-
ty go to 8; otherwise, roll 1d10 until an item stored in the 
Small Equipment Pack is scored and remove that item from 
the log sheet. If the item has been recorded as a quantity, 
the entire batch is removed. 
8.	
Large Pack: If the captain's Large Equipment Pack is emp-
ty go to 9; otherwise, roll 1d10 until an item stored in the 
Large Equipment Pack is scored and remove that item from 
the log sheet. 
9.	
Weapon:If the captain does not have an item in any of the 
weapon slots go to 10; otherwise, if there is only one item 
recorded in the weapons slots, remove the item from the 
log sheet. Otherwise, if there are two items recorded in the 
weapons slots, roll 1d6, and on a result of 1-3 the item in 
the Left slot is removed, or on a result of 4-6 it the item in 
the Right slot is removed. 
10.	 Armour: Roll 1d6 until an item stored in an Armour slot is 
scored and remove that item from the log sheet. Howev-
er, if all of the captain's Armour slots are empty go back 
through the list of results in the reverse order, i.e. from 9 
through to 1, until one can be applied. If you end back at 
result 1 and cannot fulfil its instructions, this event comes 
to an end and you can continue with the game.

Romance
Love is in the air. You're besotted with someone you've just met 
and can't stop thinking about them. They feel the same way and 
the pair of you can't stop smiling at one another. 
If this event was triggered from a trigger arrow, place a line 
through the date entry and delete its trigger arrow g from the 
star date; it no longer applies; then read on.
The captain meets someone and is head over heels in love (+1 
Karma). For a while they put everything on hold to enjoy the 
romance. Sadly the relationship doesn’t last long and they split 
up. There are some tears, but the breakup appears to be a mu-
tual decision.
Mark off 10+3d10 days on the star chart to determine how long 
the romance lasted. Then test BREAKUP below, to see how the 
captain's lover really felt about the breakup. 
BREAKUP - Test: Int - the number of days the romance lasted [S: 
The lover is okay with the breakup] [F: The lover is bitter about 
the breakup, see Bitter below] (Aware)
Bitter: Shade the star date 1d3 months and 1d10 days in the 
future. Then make the following date entry: "[DATE] After a 
breakup an old flame seeks revenge, see the Revenge event.”
Rumour
You pick up a rumour and spend a little time validating if it is true 
or not; and are excited to find out that it is.
-1d3 AP. Roll 1d10 on the Rumour Chart below, to see what has 
been discovered and how to deal with it.
Special POIs
Some of the results will require you to add a point of interest 
to a random star system and a random zone (see Random Star 
Systems and Zones for instruction of how to do this). 
When you add the special point of interest 
(its icon is shown on the right), it must be in 
an empty zone. If the star system has already 
been generated and the targeted zone already 
has a point of interest, roll again until an emp-
ty zone is generated. 
Do not name the point of interest in the usual way, instead add the 
number you scored on the Rumour Chart, followed by the name 
of the rumour; and then add at the end "see the Rumour event". 
For instance:  if you rolled a 6 It will look something like this:
 
(6) Special Water World
See the Rumour event
Then, when the captain visits the zone later in the game, you 
will have a reference to which special point of interest you 
need to look up on the Rumour Chart.

ing in space. You perform a short range scan and it reveals high 
readings of metal, plastic, plasma, radiation, and traces of fuel

it is made up of salvage material.
Roll 1d10+10 to determine how many units of salvage you may 
add to the ship's cargo hold (space permitting). Then, you may 
perform the TRANSFER CARGO test below to transfer the cargo 
to the captain's starship. You may transfer as much, or as little 
of the cargo you like that is available.

Ship Attacks
From out of nowhere a starship appears and begins an attack se-
quence. You raise the shields and prepare for the onslaught.
See the Space Battle event.
Shipmates
The starship's long range scanners pick up a number of escape 
pods floating in space. They're drifting awfully close to a zone with 
a high density of meteoroids. You run a simulation and they're due 
to intercept the zone within days. Each pod has a life sign; howev-
er, in the meteoroid zone that will be a different story!
If you wish to save the escape pods before they're destroyed 
in the meteoroid zone you must perform the TRACTOR BEAM 
test below to secure them onboard. There are 1d10+10 escape 
pods to rescue in total. You may perform the test as many times 
as you like, or until all of the escape pods have been rescued or 
destroyed. For each escape pod you rescue either add a passen-
ger, or a crew member to the log sheet (see below). 
TRACTOR BEAM - Test: Int -20, +/- CM, +/- DT [S: -1 AP, -1 PL, 
1d3 escape pod saved, add passengers or crew] [F: -1d3 AP, 
-1d3 PL, 1d3 escape pods destroyed] (Pilot)
Adding A Passenger: To add a passenger, roll for a random star 
system and then add 1 to its value on the passenger manifest. 
The star system does not need to have been generated in order 
to add a passenger.
Adding A Crew Member: To add a crew member, roll 1d10 to 
determine the type of crew they are: 1-2 Bridge, 3 Engineers, 4 
Mining Ops, 5 Navigators, 6-7 Pilots, 8 Security, 9 Smugglers, 10 
Transport. You may decide to add a crew member as a passenger 
instead after you have determined the type of crew they are.

Shortages
Across the galaxy there are shortages and the majority of traders 
are having problems getting hold of starships, modifications, or 
certain types of cargo.
Using the numbers at the top of the Economy Sheet, roll 1d100 
to select what commodity is affected. The targeted commod-
ity is now hard to find and its price has rocketed throughout the 
galaxy. Using table (GB) C - Cargo Prices reset the affected 
commodity's buy and sell value for all star systems that have 
been added to the economy sheet using the +4$ row. 
Slavery
The judge reads out your sentence and you're condemned to 
spend the rest of your life in slavery. You was hoping for Incarcer-
ation. However, you know the punishment is far better than facing 
a trial by combat. The security droids holding you, march you to a 
holding cell and from there you're transported to a slave ship. You 
have no idea where they have taken you, but after processing you 
find yourself working in a slave mine. Day after day you're taken 
to a small moon to extract minerals in an underground quarry. 
It's hard work, but at least they keep you well fed. You dream of 
escaping and hope one day your dream will come true!
Add 1d6+6 years to the Star Year box on the Star Date Chart. 
This is the number of years that have passed before an escape 
attempt can be made. For each year you add, you must apply 
the Aging modifier, which could end up triggering the Time Is 
Almost Up event. Note: If the Time Is Almost Up event is trig-
gered, or if you already have the following entry on the reverse 
of the time sheet: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and are 
feeling terrible. See the Life Expectancy event."; unfortunately 
the captain has died of old age, see the Game Over event. Any 
trigger arrows g, or other shaded dates remain in place, but do 
not activate them or deal with them. 
If the captain survives this time period of slavery reduce their 
Law to 6 and deduct -4 Rep; they can now begin trying to es-
cape captivity by performing an ESCAPE SLAVERY test each year. 
The test is made using the captain's primary Dex value with a 
-10 modifier. When performing the test, none of the captain's 
items can be used (as they have been taken from them), nor can 
any Cybercon™ implants (as they have been deactivated). Begin 
by performing the test below.
ESCAPE SLAVERY - Test: Primary Dex -10 [S: Freed] [F: Add 1 
year to the Star Year box.] (Escape)
If the test is passed successfully the captain has found a way 
to escape and has managed to reach a port in a random star 
system. Roll for a random star system. If the star system is not 
yet generated, you must generate it. The captain continues the 
game from the port in the star system. They have no posses-
sions or a starship, remove all of the following from the log 
sheet: Credits, Armour, Weapons, items in the Utility Belt, Ox-
ygen O2, Night Vision, Rations, Decoders, Power Cells, all Items 
in the Large and Small equipment packs, and the Starship from 
the log sheet. The captain does however, manage to reactivate 
their Cybercon™ implants. Next, add a trigger arrow g to the 
current star date and make the following date entry:"[DATE] 
The captain is an escaped slave from the [SYSTEM] system. 
When in zone 1 of the [SYSTEM] system, see the Tracked Down 
event." Note: You replaced [SYSTEM] with the name of the star 
system the captain suffered the Judged event in. The captain's 
only choice is to borrow some credits. See the Loan event.
If the test fails, for the next year the captain is placed in a gang 
of workers that are prone to trying to escape. Extra security is 
placed on this gang to watch for escape attempts. You then add 
1 year to the Star Year box and perform the test again.
Note: Each year until the captain has escaped you must apply the 
Aging modifier; and if the Time Is Almost Up event is triggered 
the captain has died, see the Game Over event.

Slave Ship
A large vessel appears on the stern and begins firing its weapons. 
It's a slave ship that will try to take your ship, and sell you and 
the crew into a life of slavery. Their actions are illegal and against 
galactic law, but they are little more that pirates and do not care. 
You initiate a defensive manoeuvre and must now either fight the 
slave ship or outmanoeuvre them to escape. 
Attacking The Slave Ship: If you decide to fight it out, see the 
Ship Attacks event; the slave ship gain +20 Life Support and if the 
captain's starship is destroyed or captured the captain is sold into 
slavery, see the Sold Into Slavery event. 
Escaping The Slave Ship: Other than fighting, the captain may try 
to escape. To escape the slave ship you're required to perform 
the OUTMANOEUVRE test shown below.
Whilst testing you will be generating an Escape Value (EV). The 
EV begins at 4, and if it reaches 0 the captain has managed to 
outmanoeuvre the slave ship and has escaped; and the event 
comes to an end. However, if the EV reaches 10 the captain's 
efforts to escape are thwarted and they have no choice but to 
attack the slave ship; see the Attacking The Slave Ship section 
above. You can also decide at anytime whilst trying to outma-
noeuvre, to switch tactics and just attack the slave ship, if you do 
see the Attacking The Slave Ship section above.
OUTMANOEUVRE – Test: Dex -10, +/- CM, +/- DT [S: -1 EV, -1 PL] 
[F: +1 EV, -1d3 PL] (Pilots)
Sold Into Slavery
After a few days you're transported to a slave ship. You have no 
idea where they have taken you, but after processing you find 
yourself working in a slave mine. Day after day you're taken to 
a small moon to extract minerals in an underground quarry. It's 
hard work, but at least they keep you well fed. You dream of es-
caping and hope one day your dream will come true!
Add 1d6+6 years to the Star Year box on the Star Date Chart. 
This is the number of years that have passed before an escape 
attempt can be made. For each year you add, you must apply 
the Aging modifier, which could end up triggering the Time Is 
Almost Up event. Note: If the Time Is Almost Up event is trig-
gered, or if you already have the following entry on the reverse 
of the time sheet: "[DATE] You wake in the morning and are 
feeling terrible. See the Life Expectancy event."; unfortunately 
the captain has died of old age, see the Game Over event. Any 
trigger arrows g, or other shaded dates remain in place, but do 
not activate them or deal with them. 
If the captain survives this time period of slavery, they can now 
begin trying to escape captivity by performing an ESCAPE SLAV-
ERY test each year. The test is made using the captain's primary 
Dex value with a -10 modifier. When performing the test, none 
of the captain's items can be used (as they have been taken 
from them), nor can any Cybercon™ implants (as they have 
been deactivated). Begin by performing the test below.
ESCAPE SLAVERY - Test: Primary Dex -10 [S: Freed] [F: 
Add 1 year to the Star Year box.] (Escape)
If the test is passed successfully the captain has found 
a way to escape and has managed to reach a port in a 
random star system. Roll for a random star system. If 
the star system is not yet generated, you must gener-
ate it. The captain continues the game from the port in 
the star system. They have no possessions or a starship, 
remove all of the following from the log sheet: Credits, 
Armour, Weapons, items in the Utility Belt, Oxygen O2, 
Night Vision, Rations, Decoders, Power Cells, all Items in 
the Large and Small equipment packs, and the Starship 
from the log sheet. The captain does however, manage to 
reactivate their Cybercon™ implants. Next, add a trigger 
arrow g to the current star date and make the following 
date entry:"[DATE] The captain is an escaped slave from 
the [SYSTEM] system. When in zone 1 of the [SYSTEM] 
system, see the Tracked Down event." Note: You replaced 
[SYSTEM] with the name of the star system the captain 
suffered the Sold Into Slavery event in. The captain's only 
choice is to borrow some credits. See the Loan event.
If the test fails, for the next year the captain is placed 
in a gang of workers that are prone to trying to escape. 
Extra security is placed on this gang to watch for escape 
attempts. You then add 1 year to the Star Year box and 
perform the test again.
Note: Each year until the captain has escaped you must 
apply the Aging modifier; and if the Time Is Almost Up 
event is triggered the captain has died, see the Game 
Over event.

Something To Hide
You're stuck in a line. It's crowded today and there are a bunch 
of security guards limiting the number of individuals into this 
part of the port. When you're almost at the front, you spot a 
guy from earlier; he had tried to push in front of you and you 
had an argument with him. It escalated into a pushing contest, 
until eventually he walked off. You thought he had gone to the 
back, but now you see him at the front. He must have pushed in 
up ahead when you wasn't paying attention. You shout out and 
he turns, and then you spot something that doesn't appear quite 
right. You think you've spotted a mutation.
See the Mutant event.
